Reviewer: Traced the control flow from the tool.execute.before entry point and reproduced it. src/index.ts:3695 runs enforcePrWorkflowToolBefore, then delegationGateHooks.toolBefore, which for a coder Task calls prepareCoderScope (delegation-gate.ts:3387 for the disabled-gate path and :3967 for the enabled path). prepareCoderScope (delegation-gate.ts:266-282) does `const plan = await loadPlanJsonOnly(directory); if (!plan) { ... consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration(...) ... }`. consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration has exactly one caller in all of src/ (delegation-gate.ts:285), and createPrFeedbackScopeBinding likewise one (delegation-gate.ts:306) — both inside that branch. When a plan IS loaded, execution falls through to resolveDelegatedPlanTaskId + the plan-membership gate (delegation-gate.ts:346-352) and the PR-feedback declaration is never read. My first probe attempt accidentally DISPROVED the finding because loadPlanJsonOnly returns null for a schema-invalid plan.json (plan/manager.ts:367-378) — I had written a malformed plan, which routed back into the !plan branch. With a schema-valid plan the finding reproduces exactly. This matters because it is also the reason the finding is easy to miss.

Known: ...'.
- GREP consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration / createPrFeedbackScopeBinding across src/ — one production caller each, both at delegation-gate.ts:285 and :306. No second path.
- READ src/index.ts:3676-3708 — production ordering: guardrails -> scope-guard -> enforcePrWorkflowToolBefore -> delegationGateHooks.toolBefore. prepareCoderScope always runs for a coder Task.

Known: 1.1, 1.2.`, an id colliding with a plan task throws SCOPE_CONFLICT, and an accidentally-overlapping id silently binds under plan authority with the declaration left unconsumed.

Counter-evidence examined:

- `tests/unit/hooks/pr-feedback-scope-controller.test.ts:72` — `test('authorizes exactly one planless coder Task and enforces its bound files', async () => {`
- `docs/releases/pending/pr-workflow-gate-capability-contract.md:15` — `coder Tasks work without fabricating an implementation plan. Active bindings`
- `src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:4147` — `await assertPlanCriticApprovedForExecution(directory, plan);`
- `.opencode/skills/swarm-pr-feedback/SKILL.md:274` — `Do not create a synthetic `save_plan` merely to authorize feedback work, and do not use `declare_scope`; those tools belong to the normal implementation-plan lifecycle. There is no one-file or single- …`
- `https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm/issues/2469` — `Consume an authenticated PR_FEEDBACK scope declaration even when .swarm/plan.json exists (read the declaration before generic plan-workflow preflight, including the generic Stage-A check that runs bef …`

Symptom: In any repo that has ever run save_plan (plan.json is never deleted), a /swarm pr-feedback session that has completed immutable feedback verification and called prepare_pr_feedback_scope cannot dispatch the coder that applies the fix — the Task is rejected with SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED listing unrelated implementation-plan task ids, or SCOPE_CONFLICT against the plan's files_touched — leaving no sanctioned path to close a single feedback item.

Fix direction: Resolve the authenticated PR_FEEDBACK declaration before the plan branch: in prepareCoderScope, attempt consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration for a strict task_id regardless of whether loadPlanJsonOnly returned a plan, and when it resolves return the pr_feedback binding (with plan: null / an explicit binding discriminator) so plan membership, plan-file authority and the plan-critic execution gate are bypassed for that dispatch — every existing PR_FEEDBACK verification, one-shot consumption, revision-digest and file-conflict guard staying in force. Pin it with a plan-present fixture in tests/unit/hooks/pr-feedback-scope-controller.test.ts.

Critic checked (first 3 of 16; the rest are in the critic file):

- src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:273-274 read: `const plan = await loadPlanJsonOnly(directory); if (!plan) {` — quotes in the finding match verbatim (finding's line numbers are 2-5 lines high; text is exact, not fabricated).
- src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:285-290: consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration(...) is lexically inside that `if (!plan)` block; src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:306 createPrFeedbackScopeBinding is likewise inside it; the block ends at line 337 with the `no valid plan found` throw.
- Exhaustive caller search, not a sample: `grep -rn consumePrFeedbackScopeDeclaration --include=*.ts src/` => exactly 2 hits (definition src/hooks/pr-workflow-gate.ts:11370, sole call src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:285). `grep -rn createPrFeedbackScopeBinding` => definition src/scope/scope-binding.ts:338 + sole call src/hooks/delegation-gate.ts:306. `grep -n prepareCoderScope -r src/` => defined at 266, called only at 3387 (disabled-gate path) and 3967 (enabled-gate path); both reach the same `if (!plan)` guard. No second consumer exists.

User impact: Any project that has a valid .swarm/plan.json — i.e. every project mid-run and every project that has not run /swarm close — cannot use the PR-feedback scope controller the skill mandates. The architect calls prepare_pr_feedback_scope, gets success:true, dispatches the coder, and is rejected with 'SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED: task_id "1.1" does not match any known plan task id. Known: 2.1, 2.2' — a message about implementation-plan tasks that have nothing to do with the PR feedback item. If the feedback task_id happens to collide with a plan task id the message becomes PLAN_CRITIC_GATE_VIOLATION, demanding plan-critic approval for PR-feedback work. In the one shape that does get through (colliding id + recorded plan-critic approval), the dispatch silently downgrades to an ordinary plan scope binding: the pr_feedback binding is never created, the declaration is never consumed, and the revision-digest / one-use protections that prepare_pr_feedback_scope reported as applied are not in force.

#### ECO-2 (MEDIUM)

**dispatch_lanes never links the host's ctx.abort to the lane sessions it creates, and the host's session cancel does not cascade to child sessions, so cancelling the parent turn leaves lanes generating (4 of 165 tool files read ctx.abort; dispatch-lanes.ts is not one)**

Lane: ecosystem. Kind: design. Verification chain: explorer HIGH → reviewer CONFIRMED HIGH (confidence 0.8) → critic DOWNGRADED MEDIUM.

Evidence (as re-read by the reviewer):

- `opencode@v1.18.3:packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:319` — `ctx.abort.addEventListener("abort", onAbort)`
- `opencode@v1.18.3:packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:339` — `yield* Effect.all([cancel, background.cancel(nextSession.id)], { discard: true })`
- `opencode@v1.18.3:packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:152` — `const cancel = Effect.fn("SessionPrompt.cancel")(function* (sessionID: SessionID) {       yield* Effect.logInfo("cancel", { "session.id": sessionID })       yield* state.cancel(sessionID)`
- (2 further citations in the verdict file)

Reviewer: Re-derived both halves. Host: abort reaches a tool only via ctx.abort; SessionPrompt.cancel touches one session's own state with no cascade, which is why the host's task tool cancels its child explicitly. Plugin: dispatch-lanes creates child sessions and never reads ctx.abort; createSwarmTool does not bridge it. Runtime-showed a swarm tool ignoring an already-aborted signal. HIGH: spend and repo writes continue after the user believes the turn stopped. Confidence 0.8 — derived from source, not run live, and a stale sweep eventually reaps orphans.

Checked: 7 verification steps recorded in the verdict file.

Critic (DOWNGRADED, MEDIUM): The host's own task tool has to write ctx.abort.addEventListener('abort', ...) plus an explicit background.cancel(child) because SessionPrompt.cancel touches one session's state and nothing else - dispatch_lanes creates child sessions the same way and reads ctx.abort nowhere, so pressing stop returns the turn while the lane prompts keep generating to their own 5-minute timeout.

Counter-evidence examined: 4 items recorded in the critic file.

Symptom: Cancelling a turn mid dispatch_lanes returns control immediately but each lane keeps generating for up to its timeout (5 minutes by default), so tokens keep being spent and lane artifacts keep landing in .swarm after the user believes the run stopped.

Fix direction: Thread the host ctx.abort into dispatch_lanes the way lint.ts and quality-budget.ts already do: on abort, fire the lane promptControllers and issue a session abort for every created lane session id before returning.

Critic checked: 10 verification steps recorded in the critic file.

User impact: Cancelling a run does not stop the work or the spend; orphaned lane sessions continue to consume tokens and may still write to .swarm and to the repo after the user believes the turn is cancelled.

Reproduce: 1) X, dispatch-lanes.ts absent. 2) `grep -n "addEventListener('abort'" src/tools/` -> 0 hits. 3) Read host tool/task.ts:310-345 at v1.18.3. 4) Live: dispatch_lanes_async with 2 lanes, abort the parent turn, then poll session.list — the lane sessions remain busy.

Optionally promote the existing MODEL CONFIG NOTE from the model-only advisory channel to a user-visible warning.

Critic checked: 10 verification steps recorded in the critic file.

User impact: The orchestrator is the highest-token, longest-running agent in the system and the first thing both installation guides tell a user to configure. Setting it does nothing: the architect silently runs on whichever model the OpenCode picker happens to hold (a free Zen model, or an expensive one the user did not budget for). - `src/quality/metrics.ts:1015` — `if (metrics.complexity_delta > thresholds.max_complexity_delta) {`

Reviewer: Re-derived the metric path end to end and ran it. computeComplexityDelta (src/quality/metrics.ts:105-131) sums estimateCyclomaticComplexity over the CURRENT content of each changed file and returns it as `delta`; computePublicApiDelta does the same for export counts (returns at line ~358). There is no git/base-revision code anywhere in src/quality/metrics.ts (grep for git\|spawn\|exec\|HEAD\|revision returns only 'basename'/'segment-based' noise) and the only caller, qualityBudget() -> _internals.computeQualityMetrics (src/tools/quality-budget.ts:123), passes no base. detectViolations (metrics.ts:1006-1020) compares that absolute total against max_complexity_delta (default 5, schema src/config/schema.ts:443) and escalates to severity 'error' above 1.5x, i.e. >7. qualityBudget() maps errorsCount>0 to verdict 'fail'. So the claimed mechanism is real and I reproduced the exact 46 figure. A test pins this as intended. Severity therefore drops from HIGH to MEDIUM: the real damage is a permanently-'fail' quality_budget verdict + evidence record that agents and the docs (installation.md calls its fail action 'Block review') tell the architect to act on, and a benchmark/gate-audit metric the repo has had to hard-exclude.

Reviewer: Re-derived with my own commands. detectRedirects is the one of five isNullDevice call sites that omits the filter, so any >, >>, &> or 2> to /dev/null becomes a WriteTarget, resolves to the absolute /dev/null, and is denied by the containment layer as an out-of-workspace write. Checked: 7 verification steps recorded in the verdict file.

Threat model: No attacker, no confidentiality or integrity loss — this is fail-closed over-blocking of correct commands, filed in the security lane. If anything it errs toward safety. The harmed party is the user whose own architect and coder are refused `cmd > /dev/null 2>&1` and `diff <(a) <(b)`. There is no privilege gain for anyone, so no HIGH/CRITICAL security severity is available; the defect's weight is denial-loop frequency.

Counter-evidence examined: 4 items recorded in the critic file.

Symptom: `bun test ... > /dev/null 2>&1` and `diff <(sort a) <(sort b)` are refused as an unauthorised write outside the workspace / an unparseable command, including when the agent is following this project's own bundled skills.

Fix direction: Apply the existing `isNullDevice(path)` filter inside detectRedirects before the `results.push` at shell-write-detect.ts:492 (matching the four sibling call sites), and stop treating a bash-parser failure caused solely by POSIX `<(...)` / `<<<` as a hard block — recognise those forms and continue, rather than failing closed on syntax the detector simply does not model.

Critic checked: 9 verification steps recorded in the critic file.

User impact: `cmd > /dev/null 2>&1` is one of the most common shell idioms in agent-generated commands; every use by a scoped coder is refused as an unauthorised write to a path outside the workspace. `diff <(...) <(...)` is refused as unparseable. Both denials are exactly the unactionable-block pattern that drove the #1896 dispatch loop.

#### HOOKS-9 (LOW)

**agent-activity flush lock is released while the queued flush is still running: concurrent doFlush + pendingEvents double-subtraction (benign duplicate write, counter undercount)**

Reviewer: mapStdio() defaults an omitted stdin to 'pipe' on the Node path while Bun defaults to 'ignore' (bun.d.ts:6522). Runtime: under Node bunSpawn(['cat']) and sh -c 'read x' without stdin never exit, with stdin:'ignore' they do; git log, sh -c echo and npm --version exit normally on both runtimes. The three cited tools omit stdin and breach the invariant-3 text, but their children (npm audit --json, sh -c <build cmd>, git log) do not read stdin, so the claimed Desktop stall is not demonstrated; pkg-audit and build-check also carry timeouts. LOW: real divergence plus contract drift, not a hang.

User impact: pkg_audit / build_check / complexity_hotspots may stall until timeout on OpenCode Desktop (Node).

#### JOURNEY-10 (LOW)

**Knowledge health's 'stale plugin cache' warning is driven purely by a version-check cache comparison (never a filesystem check), so it fires and recommends `bunx opencode-swarm update` even when the diagnose report's own 'Plugin Caches' row shows all 4 known cache locations absent and `update` then finds nothing to clear**

Lane: journey. Kind: ux. Verification chain: explorer LOW → reviewer CONFIRMED LOW.

- `src/services/knowledge-diagnostics.ts:243` — `return compareVersions(cache.npmLatest, version) > 0 ? 'stale' : 'fresh';`
- `src/services/knowledge-diagnostics.ts:849` — `'stale plugin cache — run `bunx opencode-swarm update` (knowledge tools may be running old code)',`
- `src/services/diagnose-service.ts:1350` — `name: 'Plugin Caches',`
- (1 further citations in the verdict file)

Reviewer: Fully reproduced end to end on the actual built plugin: the two checks are independently computed (a pure version compare vs. a real filesystem inventory) and can legitimately disagree, which they do for anyone who never went through OpenCode's own npm-package caching (checkout/global installs) — the report then sends them to a command that reports nothing to clear. One overstatement in the candidate's own hypothesis: '(knowledge tools may be running old code)' is not really a nonsensical split-version claim — knowledge tools ship in the same bundle as the check, so if the check's version is old, so are they; the message is consistent on that point, just misleadingly worded as a 'cache' problem when it's actually 'you are running an outdated published version.' Kept LOW: cosmetic self-contradiction in diagnostic wording, not a functional break — the underlying 'update available' signal is real and actionable (restart OpenCode / reinstall), only the specific 'run bunx opencode-swarm update' remedy is dead when no OpenCode cache exists.

User impact: The health report contradicts itself on the same screen and sends the user to a command that reports there is nothing to clear. Users who install globally or from a checkout — no OpenCode cache at all — see a permanent ⚠️ on their knowledge subsystem with a remedy that can never resolve it, and reasonably conclude the knowledge system is broken.

#### MAIN-9 (LOW)

**Not a duplicate of BASE-5, but a derivative of the same root cause: because opencode-swarm.schema.json is currently stale against its generator (BASE-5), the unconditional build-time regen in scripts/generate-config-schema.ts (invoked from package.json `build` step 2, and from `prepare` which `bun install` runs automatically per contributing.md step 1) silently rewrites the tracked schema file in every fresh clone's working tree; no CI job diffs the tree after build, so nothing catches it. The candidate's 'depends on which zod resolves' framing is unsupported — resolution is deterministic.**

Lane: main. Kind: drift. Verification chain: explorer MEDIUM → reviewer CONFIRMED LOW. Related issues: #2436.

- `package.json:93` — `"build": "bun run clean && bun run scripts/generate-config-schema.ts && bun run scripts/copy-grammars.ts && bun build src/index.ts ..."`
- `package.json:108` — `"prepare": "bun run build",`
- `contributing.md:29` — ``bun install` builds it automatically via the `prepare` script, so a fresh clone is runnable.`
- (4 further citations in the verdict file)

Reviewer: Re-derived independently of MAIN-9's own text. This is NOT a restatement of BASE-5 (which is about the artifact's CONTENT being stale/wrong and CI reporting it as an unenforced error) -- it identifies a different consequence of the SAME root drift: the standard, documented contributor workflow (bun install -> prepare -> build; and Tier 5's explicit `bun run build`) unconditionally re-triggers the generator, and because the committed file currently differs from generator output (BASE-5's 5 hunks, reproduced here independently), that build step actually rewrites a tracked file in the working tree as an undocumented side effect -- with no CI check to catch it. This is a genuine, verified increment (workflow/DX hygiene: routine commands dirty git status with no warning to the contributor, docstring rationale notwithstanding, since contributing.md never mentions this). It is causally downstream of BASE-5 and will stop recurring once BASE-5's stale artifact is regenerated and committed, so I score it LOW rather than MEDIUM: no runtime/correctness impact, no broken CI, self-healing at publish time (release-and-publish.yml builds fresh before `npm publish`, so the shipped package artifact is always current regardless of tracked-file staleness). I also correct the candidate's speculative 'depends on which zod resolves' framing -- resolution is deterministic, not a source of nondeterminism.

Reviewer: The premise checks out exactly against Node's own rimraf implementation, which I dumped at runtime: maxRetries defaults to 0 and the sync path makes exactly one attempt, so an AV/indexer handle is fatal to the whole recursive removal. #### PORT-009 (LOW)

**quality metrics' relative-path strip is separator- and depth-naive: on Windows it never strips (globs run against an absolute path), on POSIX it strips to the basename — so include/exclude glob results differ by platform (loop.ts and partition-common.ts are not defects)**

Reviewer: Runtime-simulated with path.win32: on Windows the `${dirPath}/` needle never occurs so relativePath stays absolute, while on POSIX it degrades to the basename. globMatches and shouldExcludeFile slash-normalise but never re-relativise, so configured include/exclude globs evaluate against structurally different strings per platform. #### PORT-011 (LOW)

**safeChildEnv forwards HOME but no Windows home variable (USERPROFILE/HOMEDRIVE/HOMEPATH), so predicate children on Windows lose the git global config (safe.directory, identity, longpaths) that the same predicate sees on POSIX**

Lane: portability. Kind: portability. Verification chain: explorer LOW → reviewer CONFIRMED LOW.

Reviewer: Re-derived: safeChildEnv is a total replacement env (mergeEnvForChild honors an explicit base), and it forwards the POSIX home variable but no Windows equivalent. I proved on Linux that stripping every home variable makes git blind to the global config and makes a `safe.directory`-excepted repo fail with exit 128 - the same child git that changedPaths() and any `tool: git ...` predicate run. **The 30 s-cached freshness walk runs inside the awaited system-prompt transform, adding a bounded whole-workspace readdir+stat (193-329 ms here, capped at walk_budget_ms) to the first agent turn after each TTL expiry — documented behaviour, and required to decide suppression**

#### testsci-1-NEW-1 (LOW)

**The merge-queue integration loop (ci.yml:797) and run-coverage-gate.sh:151 call `bun test` directly, so a synchronous or top-level-await hang - neither of which Bun's --timeout can interrupt - runs until the job's 10-/30-minute budget instead of exiting 124 with [TIMEOUT] as the unit job's wrapper does**

Lane: reviewnew. Kind: bug. Verification chain: explorer LOW → reviewer CONFIRMED LOW.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:797` — `bun --smol test "$f" --timeout 120000 > "$tmp" 2>&1 \|\| exit_code=$?`
- `scripts/ci/run-coverage-gate.sh:151` — `bun test --isolate --coverage --timeout 60000 "$test_file" > "$tmpout" 2>&1 \|\| exit_code=$?`

- (1 further citations in the verdict file)

Reviewer: Every structural claim checks out against the workflow and both scripts, and I reproduced the behavioural core: Bun's --timeout does not fire for a synchronous loop or a top-level-await stall, SIGTERM does not end them, and only the unit job's wrapper turns them into exit 124 with a [TIMEOUT] annotation. The integration and coverage loops call bun directly, so such a file burns the 10-/30-minute job budget with no per-file annotation and, since both jobs are merge-queue-only, evicts the PR from the queue. Rare class, small blast radius, no user-facing effect: LOW is right.

User impact: A hung integration/coverage file costs the full job budget and a queue re-run with no file-level diagnostic; rare hang class, so LOW.

#### STATE-10 (LOW)

**Four issue-trace receipt writers do temp+rename with no fsync, no bounded rename retry, and no failure cleanup — a rename error leaves a permanently un-quarantinable constant-named .tmp and returns a raw errno from a gate-unblocking tool**

Lane: state. Kind: portability. Verification chain: explorer MEDIUM → reviewer CONFIRMED LOW. Related issues: #2391.

Reviewer: The mechanics are exactly as stated and I reproduced the temp-leak and opaque-error at runtime. But the severity is overstated on three counts. (1) The constant-name temp is not an anomaly of these four — it is an explicitly registered repo-wide grammar with 21 declared producers. (2) The stated consequence is backwards: dot-constant-tmp is quarantineEligible:false, so swarm-residue PRESERVES the leftover rather than quarantining it. (3) The rename-retry gap is Windows-only (POSIX rename-over-existing never returns EPERM/EBUSY) and the failure is loud and retryable by the agent, not data loss. Real residual defect: a gate-unblocking write with no fsync, no bounded retry, no temp cleanup, and a temp name two concurrent callers share.

User impact: On Windows the issue-trace workflow can fail to record its review receipt because of a transient AV/indexer lock, blocking the PR handoff with an opaque error; a leftover .tmp is also left behind for the residue sweep to quarantine.

### 3.4 Severities the report-level critic disputes

An independent critic read this report to attack its judgement rather than its arithmetic, and disputed four
severities and one counting decision. Those disputes are recorded here rather than applied, because a severity in
section 3 is the verdict of a reviewer and a critic who each re-derived the finding from source, and overriding
that from the synthesis would erase the gate that produced it. A reader weighing remediation order should read both.

| Finding | Section 3 says | The report critic argues | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| TOOLS-1 | **Applied.** Merged into HOST-1 and no longer listed separately | Not an independent finding; merge into HOST-1 | Applied on the critic's ruling. Its argument: the rule below protects a severity *reached by a gate*, and this one was retracted by a later gate of the same kind — critic batch c14, holding a runtime replay batch c04 did not have, concluded the mechanism was wrong for every agent this plugin ships and said the two must be merged. Folding it therefore honours the later gate rather than overriding the earlier one, and leaving it would have preserved a verdict the gate itself withdrew. |
| HOOKS-1 | HIGH | MEDIUM | The defect requires an operator to set a documented opt-out that defaults to on. This report discounted the subprocess finding from critical to high partly because no evidence showed any user runs the plugin on that host; the same discount is not applied here. |
| SEC2-6 | MEDIUM, reviewer downgraded from high | HIGH | A protected-path control fails open on case-insensitive volumes, which is the default on the most common development platform. It was held at medium because the case-folding could not be observed on this host — yet a portability finding is rated high on source reading alone for a platform this audit also could not run. |
| main-2-NEW-1 | LOW | MEDIUM | The stated reason for low — the user can restore their own settings by hand — covers only half the finding. The other half leaves the host's built-in agents permanently disabled after uninstall with no command that restores them. |
| MAIN-10 and HOOKS-7 | Two findings, critical and high | One defect | They share the host mechanism, most of their evidence and their entire fix. Merging them would make the distinct-defect count 29 rather than 30. The report merged a different pair on a narrower relation, so the policy is applied inconsistently. |

The critic was asked to rule on whether recording these rather than applying them is discipline or evasion, and
answered: discipline for three, evasion for one. The one is TOOLS-1, applied above, on the ground that a later gate
had already retracted the earlier gate's verdict. For HOOKS-1, SEC2-6 and main-2-NEW-1 it agreed the disputes should
be recorded and not applied, noting that its own challenges there are calibration arguments rather than new evidence —
it did not reproduce the case-folding on a case-insensitive volume, and produced no evidence that any user disables
compaction. Those arguments turn on applying one evidentiary standard consistently, which is a fair charge; whether
the answer is to raise one rating or lower the other is left visible here rather than settled silently.

MAIN-10 and HOOKS-7 remain counted separately. No gate ruled on whether they are one defect, so nothing is overridden
either way, and unlike TOOLS-1 the split leaves no refuted mechanism in circulation — only a distinct-defect count
that would move from thirty to twenty-nine. The relationship is stated on both findings so a reader can judge it.

## 4. Subsystem summaries and coverage gaps

### Baseline health and build/test/check status (`baseline`)

Root-caused the reproduced Node-vs-Bun init orphan-recovery divergence to a cross-runtime contract defect in bunSpawn's Node fallback: streamFromNode attaches its 'data'/'end' listeners lazily on the first .text() call, but Node ends the child's stdout during teardown, so every one of the repo's 18 read-after-exit call sites gets a promise that never settles and loses the bytes. Proved with an instrumented copy of dist/index.js (child exits 0 at 14 ms, stdout.text() still pending 8 s later under Node; resolves at 8 ms under Bun on the same bundle), an strace showing the git subprocess really does run, a 5-line Node/Bun A-B on the TypeScript source, and a reduction to plain node:child_process. Consequence: init orphan recovery is 100% inert on Node hosts - no lane-branch cleanup, no orphan-worktree removal, no `git worktree prune` - and the same defect sits in both worktree runGit helpers (36 call sites in merge.ts) and 14 sites in worktree-isolation.ts. No test can reach the path because the suite runs only under Bun. Rebuilt the lost baseline-health record on top of that: a stale shipped JSON schema that drift:check reports at error severity while exiting 0, 48 deterministic batch-only test failures that pass per-file, a TESTING.md CI table describing a pipeline that no longer exists, a cross-contamination check emitting 253 unactionable annotations per run against a dead CI model, one dead invariant-8 helper the lint gate lets through, and four permanently non-blocking baselines.

Contracts observed:

- bunSpawn (src/utils/bun-compat.ts:887) must present one BunCompatSubprocess contract on both runtimes: {stdout, stderr, exited, exitCode, signalCode, spawnError, kill, killTree}. VIOLATED on the Node branch - stdout/stderr may only be read BEFORE the child is reaped; nothing in the type or docs states that precondition, and 18/18 read-after-exit call sites get it wrong.
- runInitOrphanRecovery (src/hooks/init-orphan-recovery.ts:384) runs from the wrapper-owned post-resolution queue, wraps each scan in withTimeout, logs non-fatally, writes .swarm/advisories/init-orphan-recovery.json, and surfaces it once per session via createInitOrphanRecoveryAdvisoryHook (src/index.ts:2052 -> 3414). Fail-open behaviour holds; the recovery work itself never runs on Node.
- OWNERSHIP_TAG_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000 bounds the two subprocess-backed scans (init-orphan-recovery.ts:540, :604); INIT_ORPHAN_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000 bounds the three synchronous fs scans (:627, :641, :680) where the timeout is explicitly documented as observability only, not interrupt capability.
- CI unit gate = find every *.test.ts, subtract scripts/ci/quarantined-tests.txt, round-robin into 6 shards, one process per file with 2 retries (ci.yml:400-476). TESTING.md's step table and scripts/check-cross-contamination.ts's HOOK_STEP_GLOBS both encode an older per-directory model.
- drift:check is soft-warn by default (exit 0) unless the repo variable DRIFT_CHECK_ENFORCE is set (drift-check.yml:55, drift-check.ts:1666); the config-schema detector emits severity 'error' regardless.

Coverage gaps:

- BASE-1/BASE-3 bear on runtime portability generally (the portability lane owns dist-level invariant-2 checks); I proved the primitive and one end-to-end consumer but did not exercise a real delegation/worktree provisioning cycle under Node - a reviewer should.
- Init structure and multi-instance behaviour are the init lane's: I only used init as the vehicle to reach the post-resolution orphan-recovery task and did not audit the queue itself.
- Init latency is the perf lane's: my measurements (server() 82-137 ms, import ~1.0 s under Node) are incidental and are not offered as findings.
- .swarm path census and retention are the state lane's: I observed .swarm/advisories/init-orphan-recovery.json being written and then deleted by the advisory hook, and .swarm-worktrees/<sessionId>/ never being reclaimed on Node (BASE-2), but did not census the tree.
- The first-run CLI journey is the journey lane's: the misleading 'Orphan recovery timed out' advisory the architect sees on turn 1 of every Node session is theirs to judge for wording.
- BASE-7 and BASE-8 touch CI workflow structure, which is the testsci lane's: I raise them only as documentation/gate drift discoverable from the baseline check record, and defer the pipeline design question to that lane. BASE-10's per-gate ratchet design is likewise theirs.
- tests/unit/build's 7 batch failures (discovery-profiles-adversarial.test.ts) are carried from the dead agent's S/test-build.log and were NOT re-run by me (68 s); config and cli were both re-derived.
- I did not determine WHEN the streamFromNode laziness was introduced - `git blame` collapses to the release merge commit 46053f0 (2026-08-26) on a shallow history, so I cannot say whether BASE-1 is a regression or has always been present.

### Commands, skills, bundled-skill sync (`commands`)

Registry (154 keys), tool-policy derivation, 93 OpenCode shortcuts, CLI run(), bundled-skill sync and mirror contracts are internally coherent: drift-check is clean and the four skill wiring tests pass (69/69). Defects sit at cross-file seams: (1) the architect prompt's own delegation template names SKILLS paths that exist only in this repo while a MANDATORY reference gate throws on a missing file and bundled fallbacks are excluded from discovery; (2) opencode-swarm-internal skills (bun:test, AGENTS.md, biome/package-check) are bundled into every consumer project and the prompt mandates injecting them; (3) /swarm ci-simulate hardcodes this repo's bun scripts yet is agent-invocable; (4) /swarm analyze emits a MODE signal no architect section consumes; (5) seven bundled skills (~150KB) are unreachable in OpenCode per the repo's own doc; (6) help/tool-policy text claims read-only routing while 'agent' policy covers mutating/subprocess commands; (7) docs/commands.md omits 29 registry commands; (8) init comment misstates sync bounds.

- COMMAND_REGISTRY is SSOT; toolPolicy derives z.enum/ALLOWLIST/HUMAN_ONLY (tool-policy.ts); 93 swarm-<cmd> shortcuts hand-maintained at src/index.ts:2921-3377 (parity test, only 'help' exempt)

### Config, schema, CLI (`config`)

Mapped config loading (loader.ts recovery ladder), schema/docs generation (verified byte-identical to regeneration) and the Bun-only CLI. Reproduced in isolated XDG dirs: (1) `install` replaces an unparseable ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (BOM/UTF-16/typo) with a minimal file, destroying providers/MCP/other plugins — the path docs recommend for 'architect not visible'; (2) `install` leaves version-pinned packages/opencode-swarm@<semver> caches (invariant 12) while `update` clears them. Three documented config samples fail schema/JSON validation and push users into the guardrails-default ladder. `/swarm diagnose` and config-doctor read only the project (or one) config, so a corrupt user-level config is reported green. The CLI bundle crashes under Node (verified) although getting-started advertises an npm-only path. Smaller: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR ignored by plugin lookups; env-var table incomplete; secure() wipes/mislabels guardrails when one file is corrupt; init writes .swarm/ into any opened directory.

Contracts observed:

- User config <XDG_CONFIG_HOME\|~/.config>/opencode/opencode-swarm.json; project <dir>/.opencode/opencode-swarm.json; strict JSON.parse, 100KB cap, BOM stripped (loader.ts:51-129); prompts <config>/opencode/opencode-swarm/{agent}[_append].md

### Configuration key census (`configcensus`)

Script-driven census of all 784 declared config key paths (72 top-level) from PluginConfigSchema. 40 keys have no production reader, including three whole quality gates, the entire `parallelization` section (its `createDispatcher` factory has no production caller), and four `skill_opt` caps the code itself documents as unused. 61 of the 72 top-level keys resolve to undefined for a user with no config file (optional, no section default), so every nested default is latent: `/swarm config` on a fresh project prints only 6 sections, and a consumer that tests truthiness instead of `!== false` silently inverts a `true` default (confirmed in `/swarm diagnose`, which reports 'Curator: Disabled' for a default install). Validation fails open and, critically, SILENT: `advisoryWarn` never writes to stdout/stderr, so a project with an unparseable config produces exactly one line at startup ('running v7.160.2') while the whole config is discarded; a typo inside a non-strict section produces no diagnostic at all. `/swarm diagnose` then prints a green 'Plugin config: Valid configuration loaded' next to a red 'Config Parseability ... not valid JSON'. The shipped opencode-swarm.schema.json is stale against its own generator (drift-check reports it as an error but is soft-warn). Docs promise six `gates.*` options that do not exist and README documents three `context_budget.scoring.weights` names that are silently replaced by defaults. Only one prompt-vs-default drift exists (the already-known turbo.lean.worktree_isolation one); the other eleven prompt default claims all check out.

Contracts observed:

- PluginConfigSchema (src/config/schema.ts:3353) declares 72 top-level keys / 784 unique paths; 66 top-level keys are .optional() with no section default, so PluginConfigSchema.parse({}) materializes only 44 leaf values (config_format_version, max_iterations, qa_retry_limit, execution_mode, inject_phase_reminders, repo_graph.*, adversarial_testing.*, turbo_mode, quiet, version_check, full_auto.*).
- opencode-swarm.schema.json contains 100% of the 784 declared paths and is byte-compared against serializeConfigSchema() by scripts/drift-check.ts detectConfigSchemaDrift (severity 'error', soft-warn unless DRIFT_CHECK_ENFORCE=1); the marker-delimited generated table in docs/configuration.md is currently in sync.
- Every config diagnostic routes through advisoryWarn (src/services/warning-buffer.ts:152) which buffers for /swarm diagnose and logs only under OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1; it never writes stdout/stderr. Loader recovery ladder labels: none \| sanitized_values \| stripped_keys \| guardrails_defaults.
- Only 3 of 6 quality gates read config: syntax_check (src/tools/syntax-check.ts:135), sast_scan (src/tools/sast-scan.ts:375), quality_budget (src/tools/pre-check-batch.ts:786). sanitizeGatesConfig (src/config/loader.ts:245-279) strips unknown gate sub-keys against GATE_CONFIG_KNOWN_SECTION_KEYS (src/config/schema.ts:455).
- constants.ts DEFAULT_* mirrors: DEFAULT_SCORING_CONFIG and DEFAULT_WORKTREE_ISOLATION_CONFIG match the schema exactly; DEFAULT_LEAN_TURBO_CONFIG diverges on deps_strategy; SLOP_DETECTOR_DEFAULTS / INCREMENTAL_VERIFY_DEFAULTS / COMPACTION_DEFAULTS / KNOWLEDGE_UNIFIED_INJECTION_TOKENS_DEFAULT have no consumer.

Coverage gaps:

- Positive test coverage per key is a word-level heuristic and is NOT claimed: 'max_coders' matches 89 test lines because Lean Turbo has an unrelated max_parallel_coders. Only the negative signal is asserted (39 canonical keys with no leaf-name occurrence in any test file). Proving 'a non-default value is exercised' needs per-test config-literal parsing, which was not built.
- src/config/schema.ts was read only at the ~60 sites quoted; the shape census is script-derived and complete, but the 4086 lines of .describe()/comment prose were not read line by line.
- .refine/.superRefine cross-key constraints are invisible to z.toJSONSchema and were not enumerated, so a key can appear reachable in the table yet be rejected by a cross-field rule.
- Dynamic readers of the form config[section][computedKey] can be missed by the chain index. One such pattern was positively confirmed as a real reader (EVENT_CONFIG_MAP → config[configFlag], src/background/pr-event-subscribers.ts:110-158, covering all seven pr_monitor.notify_* keys); others may exist.
- The 209 'undocumented' figure counts a key as documented if its bare leaf name appears anywhere in the three doc files, which over-credits documentation; the true undocumented count is higher.
- Doc-sample validation covered docs/configuration.md, README.md, docs/getting-started.md and docs/installation.md only — not docs/observability.md, docs/plan-durability.md, the .opencode/.claude skill trees, or release notes.
- The validation experiment used PROJECT-level config only; user-level config, the user+project merge order and enforceGitBinaryProvenance were left to the prior config lane (CONFIG-9).
- src/services/config-doctor.ts (2680 lines) auto-fix and backup paths were not exercised; only emitWorktreeIsolationLayeringAdvisory and the gates known-keys reuse were read.
- No Windows or macOS host: %LOCALAPPDATA% / ~/Library config-path behaviour and the npm cmd-shim + bun shebang interaction were not exercised.
- The e2e run used dist/index.js as built in this workspace; `bun run build` was deliberately not run (it rewrites the tracked schema artifact), so dist may lag the current src by whatever the last build captured.

### Gate denial ergonomics (`denials`)

Census of every gate denial the model can receive: 126 distinct code tokens behind 598 distinct denial message sites. Only 45/598 message sites (7.5%) name a concrete next call; 30/126 codes are ACTIONABLE at their best variant, 30 DIRECTIONAL, 66 OPAQUE at every site. Zero codes appear in README.md, 13 in any agent prompt, 37 have no test, no doc and no prompt mention. The load-bearing defects are structural, not prose: (1) the gate-denial tracker classifies by the text before the first colon, so 446 distinct BLOCKED messages (299 of them in pr-workflow-gate.ts) share one streak bucket while one root cause fragments across up to 9 code tokens, making the warn text ('denial #N with the same cause') false in both directions; (2) the 3/5 ladder is invocation-scoped and every architect turn boundary calls beginInvocation -> clearInvocationActionCircuits, so the multi-turn loop it was built for (#1896: 20-30 tries across two compactions) can never reach a rung; (3) AuthorityDecision.recovery ('declare_scope'\|'save_plan') is computed at 6 deny sites and has zero readers, so the plugin discards the next call for its highest-traffic write denial; (4) /swarm guardrail explain and /swarm guardrail reset exist and are referenced 0 times outside the command registry; (5) the shell-write SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED collapses three unrelated causes into one message that names a tool only the architect can call, and unlike its scope-guard twin pushes no advisory to the architect; (6) the most actionable message in the codebase, ACCEPTANCE_FIELD_COVERAGE_MISMATCH, is self-declared structurally unreachable. Nine denial clusters identified where one problem presents as 5-16 different codes in sequence. Five families exercised end-to-end against the real hooks.

Warn at 3, STOP at 5 (:64,:67); UNCLASSIFIED gets hardStopThreshold=MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (:308-311); decoration is append-only and the same Error object is rethrown (src/index.ts:4032).
- Fail-closed toolBefore chain, in order (src/index.ts:3675-3775): 1 guardrails.toolBefore, 2 scopeGuardHook.toolBefore, 3 enforcePrWorkflowToolBefore, 4 delegationGateHooks.toolBefore, 5 fullAutoDelegationHook, 6 fullAutoPermissionHook, 7 knowledgeApplicationGateBefore, 7b skillPropagationGateBefore. Every throw from these lands on the single catch at src/index.ts:3976 which calls recordDeniedToolCall then noteGateDenial then rethrows.
- Recovery-clause conventions in use, none enforced: 'ACTION[architect]: <call>' at 23 sites in 6 files; denyWithArchitectAdvisory (src/hooks/scope-guard.ts:408-431) additionally pushes '[SCOPE GUARD] <message>' into the architect session before throwing; src/hooks/guardrails/tool-before.ts has zero pushAdvisory/injectAdvisory calls.

### ecosystem (`ecosystem`)

Read OpenCode v1.18.3's plugin docs (plugins.mdx, custom-tools.mdx, permissions.mdx, ecosystem.mdx, config.mdx) and the host source that implements them. opencode-swarm gets the load-bearing shape right — v1 {id,server} default export, id == package name, agents/commands via the config hook exactly as the host's own test fixture does, in-place mutation of the chat transform arrays, throw-to-block in tool.execute.before. Where it diverges it does so by re-implementing host affordances it never touches: ctx.ask is never called anywhere in src/ although the host bridges it into every plugin tool and uses it for its own write tool, so swarm_apply_patch writes files outside the user's permission.edit policy; 5 of 165 non-test src/tools files read ctx.abort and dispatch-lanes builds its own unlinked AbortController, so cancelling a turn leaves lane sessions running where the host's task tool cancels its child; the host's PluginOptions channel (plugin:[["pkg",{...}]] -> server(input,options)) is ignored in favour of a private opencode-swarm.json, so remote/managed/MDM config layers cannot reach the plugin; 120 console.* calls and zero client.app.log despite plugins.mdx:319; and createSwarmTool turns every throw, AbortError included, into a successful JSON string so the host's tool-error state never fires. Size: 129 tools = 46,959 desc + 119,991 schema chars = 169,124 (~42K tokens), 11.2x the host's entire built-in tool description surface (15,073); the architect prompt is 137,152 chars, 8.9x the host's largest system prompt and 1.26x all fourteen combined. Because the host drops a tool only on an explicit deny, every one of the 21 agents receives all 129 tool schemas — including curator_consolidation, whose own allow-list is empty. There is no host-side tool-count, schema-size, or hook-timeout limit anywhere in the load path, so nothing rejects this; the ceiling is the model's context. Reference points read: the host's own example.ts/example-workspace.ts, its ten internal auth plugins, its test/plugin fixtures, and four community plugins named in ecosystem.mdx.

Contracts observed:

- Hooks = 21 keys (packages/plugin/src/index.ts:222-335). Dispatch is sequential per plugin and per hook (plugin/index.ts:287-291) via Effect.promise, not tryPromise. dispose runs as a scope finalizer (plugin/index.ts:261-274). config fires once with the resolved config and mutations to it are what Agent (agent/agent.ts:267) and Command (command/index.ts:90) read.
- No timeout exists anywhere in resolve -> import -> server(): plugin/loader.ts:139 and plugin/index.ts:114 are plain awaits. AGENTS.md invariant 1's claim that the host 'silently drops a plugin whose entry never resolves' is not supported by v1.18.3 source; the actual failure mode is that Plugin.state never resolves.
- A tool leaves the request only via an explicit deny: permission/index.ts:210-211 requires rule.pattern === '*' && rule.action === 'deny', applied at session/llm/request.ts:208-213. agent.tools is deprecated in favour of permission and normalizes true->allow / false->deny (core/src/v1/config/agent.ts:21-23, 69-76).
- The host bridges permission prompting, cancellation, streaming metadata, directory/worktree and output truncation into every plugin tool: tool/registry.ts:143-154 and packages/plugin/src/tool.ts:3-20.
- Per-plugin configuration is a first-class channel: Spec = Union([String, Tuple([String, Options])]) (core/src/v1/config/plugin.ts:8) -> pluginOptions (config/plugin.ts:36-38) -> server(input, load.options) (plugin/index.ts:114).
- npm plugins are version-gated by engines.opencode (plugin/shared.ts:194-205, called at loader.ts:125-131); entrypoint resolution prefers exports['./server'] then main (plugin/meta.ts:103-114); path plugins must export id, npm plugins default to package name (shared.ts:306-323).
- ToolRegistry.tools() rebuilds every tool definition and fires tool.definition per tool on every call (tool/registry.ts:305-334); SessionTools.resolve calls it once per agentic step inside prompt.ts's while(true) loop (prompt.ts:1088, 1226). agent.prompt replaces the host system prompt wholesale every request (llm/request.ts:60).

### OpenCode host contract cross-check (`hostcontract`)

Verified against a confirmed opencode v1.18.3 clone (commit 127bdb30, `git describe` = v1.18.3) with every load-bearing file re-fetched at npm-latest v1.18.26 for drift. The lane's central result: the plugin's per-agent `tools` allow/deny map is not 'additive-only', it is INERT. The only host code that reads `agent.tools` is the config decoder's `normalize()` (core/src/v1/config/agent.ts:69), which runs while parsing opencode.json — long before plugins load; `Agent.state`'s config merge (agent/agent.ts:267-294) never copies `.tools`, `Agent.Info` has no `tools` field, and tool visibility is decided solely by `Permission.disabled` over permission rulesets (permission/index.ts:210-211, llm/request.ts:213). A host-faithful replay over the plugin's own getAgentConfigs output measures 2388 intended per-agent denies and 0 enforced, across all 21 agents, with a positive control proving the replay works. Same file at v1.18.26: 0 changed lines. Second: the host's message role union is literally `Union([User, Assistant])` (schema/src/v1/session.ts:490) and `toModelMessagesEffect` has exactly two `if` branches with no else (message-v2.ts:198,244,402), so every synthetic `role:'system'` message the plugin pushes is silently discarded — host facts recorded for MAIN-10, which owns that verdict. Third: a complete 17-id host tool census versus every literal the plugin compares, isolating 5 exclusive-'Task' sites (a dead loop circuit-breaker among them) and proving normalizeToolName can never rescue them because no host tool id can contain ':' or '.' (mcp/catalog.ts:117). Plus: no `dispose` against a per-directory ScopedCache with infinite capacity; the host auto-denies `task`/`todowrite` to every subagent whose permission lacks a literal key; hook rejections are Effect defects that pass through Effect.catch (empirically confirmed on the exact host effect version); and the ephemeral 'read-only' denial list omits webfetch/websearch/skill/execute and all MCP tools.

Contracts observed:

- Host refs: primary = git clone at tag v1.18.3, S/verify/sdk-2/oc, commit 127bdb30784d508cc556c71a0f32b508a3061517, `git describe --tags` -> v1.18.3. Drift = raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/v1.18.26/<path> (8/8 HTTP 200) saved to S/host2/. npm dist-tags.latest for @opencode-ai/plugin = 1.18.26; bun.lock pins 1.18.3.
- Trigger loop (plugin/index.ts:287-292): sequential over hooks, `yield* Effect.promise(async () => fn(input, output))`, `return output` (SAME object). Return value of the handler is discarded; a rejection is an Effect DEFECT that passes Effect.catch and is caught only by catchCause/Effect.exit/run.promise. Verified empirically on effect@4.0.0-beta.83 = host catalog version (S/verify/sdk-2/effect-promise-probe.mjs).
- In-place mutation required for exactly: experimental.chat.messages.transform (prompt.ts:1255->1262, compaction.ts:350->351), experimental.chat.system.transform (llm/request.ts:69-73 -> :74,99,105), command.execute.before (prompt.ts:1460->1466). Returned-object consumed for: text.complete (processor.ts:516), session.compacting (compaction.ts:343-348), compaction.autocontinue (compaction.ts:454-471), chat.params/chat.headers (llm/request.ts:114,134), tool.definition (registry.ts:313-317). AGENTS.md invariant 10's scoping is CORRECT.
- Host tool ids (Tool.define first arg): invalid, question, bash (tool/shell/id.ts:16), read, glob, grep, edit, write, task (tool/task.ts:24 `const id = "task"`), webfetch, todowrite, websearch, skill, apply_patch, execute (code-mode.ts:12), lsp, plan_exit; plus list_mcp_resources / list_mcp_resource_templates / read_mcp_resource (session/tools.ts:27-31); plus MCP `<client>_<name>` via sanitize(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g -> '_'). No host tool id can contain ':' or '.'.
- Permission: default action for an unmatched rule is 'ask' (permission/index.ts:28-38); default AGENT ruleset is `*: allow` (agent/agent.ts:119-136). Precedence is flat concat + findLast: defaults -> built-in overrides -> top-level cfg.permission -> per-agent value.permission (agent.ts:293) -> session permission (request.ts:211). `permission.ask` HOOK has zero trigger sites at v1.18.3 and v1.18.26.
- Lifecycle: one plugin instance per DIRECTORY — Plugin.state is InstanceState.make (plugin/index.ts:130) over a ScopedCache keyed by directory with capacity Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY (effect/instance-state.ts:30-31,47-50). bootstrap.ts:37-38 runs plugin.init() before every other service precisely so plugins can mutate cfg. Entry rejection is logged only; the session-error publish is commented out (plugin/index.ts:229-234).

No finding here is VERSION-RISK-only.

### Plugin init and runtime portability (`init`)

The server() critical path is lean and bounded (repro-704 T1 62.7ms Node/Linux; 8 sync fs calls before resolution under node --trace-sync-io). Defects cluster around process-global state not keyed by directory although OpenCode instantiates the plugin per directory (lanes, tabs; lane-permissions.ts:15-17). A harness calling server() for two git workspaces plus a bare HOME in one Node process proves: the 2nd workspace is never git-excluded while .swarm/ is created there; the 2nd gets no telemetry.jsonl; HOME gains ~/.swarm/ with five entries. On the Node sidecar the sqlite adapter's run() returns undefined for parameterless SQL while /swarm link's migration reads .changes. bun-compat's Node stdin default diverges from Bun. No dispose hook; exit listeners accumulate; each lane instance replays the whole post-init queue.

Contracts observed:

- default export {id:'opencode-swarm', server}; hooks: name, agent, tool, event, config, experimental.chat.{messages,system}.transform, experimental.text.complete, experimental.session.compacting, command.execute.before, tool.execute.{before,after}, chat.message, automation; SDK 1.18.3 Hooks has dispose? but no agent/name keys (agents registered via config hook, src/index.ts:2790)

### New-user journey (exercised) (`journey`)

Executed the documented first-run path for real against dist/ with an isolated HOME: bunx opencode-swarm install/update/uninstall/--help/-v/run across five opencode.json shapes (absent, valid+other plugins, JSONC, valid-with-comma-in-string, unparseable, legacy config.json), plus loading dist/index.js under Node with a repro-704-shaped ctx and invoking swarm_command(status/diagnose/agents/preflight), get_approved_plan, repo_map and two knowledge tools. The happy path mostly works: merge semantics over an existing valid config are non-destructive, install is idempotent, uninstall --clean does exactly what it advertises, .swarm/ is git-excluded before the 1.3 MB of post-init writes land, and server() resolves in 71-127 ms with one stdout line. The damage is concentrated where the user tries to VERIFY or CONFIGURE: the architect model the docs put first in every config example is deleted before registration while /swarm agents reports it as applied (JOURNEY-1); the installer's own generated config produces 5 of the 6 warnings the plugin then shows the user (JOURNEY-3); the first-run diagnose report shows two unavoidable red X marks against a doc that says fix every X before proceeding (JOURNEY-4); the terminal roster command always says 'No agents registered' (JOURNEY-5); and the CLI's JSONC pre-processor silently rewrites string values inside strictly-valid JSON and persists them (JOURNEY-2). Runtime confirmation (not re-filed) for CONFIG-1 (unparseable overwrite, exit 0, no backup), CONFIG-2 (install misses version-pinned caches), CONFIG-5/DOCS-4 (node dist/cli/index.js dies with 'TypeError: __require is not a function'), and DOCS-12 (README:27 vs :170).

Contracts observed:

- CLI verbs are exactly: install (also the no-arg default), update, uninstall, run <subcommand>, -h/--help, -v/--version (src/cli/index.ts:794-819). There is NO `doctor` CLI verb; `doctor` exists only as a /swarm registry alias and a `run` subcommand.
- Config locations: getPluginConfigDir() = $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\|\|~/.config + /opencode; OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH=<dir>/opencode.json, PLUGIN_CONFIG_PATH=<dir>/opencode-swarm.json, PROMPTS_DIR=<dir>/opencode-swarm/. install writes all three; it never writes anything into the project.
- install merge semantics on a PARSEABLE opencode.json are additive and non-destructive: plugin array filtered of opencode-swarm* then appended; agent.explore/agent.general spread-merged with disable:true; all other top-level keys preserved verbatim (verified with theme/model/mcp/$schema/agent.build).
- Registered plugin surface under Node against a fresh project: 21 agents (1 primary `architect` with model deleted, 20 subagents), 129 tools, 10 hooks; topLevelKeys = name,agent,tool,event,config,experimental.chat.messages.transform,experimental.text.complete,experimental.chat.system.transform,experimental.session.compacting,command.execute.before,tool.execute.before,tool.execute.after,chat.message,automation.
- All 20 subagent defaults resolve to opencode/* ids (big-pickle x9, gpt-5-nano x9, minimax-m2.5-free for coder) and every fallback_models chain the installer writes is opencode/* only; per-agent overrides DO take effect for subagents (coder -> anthropic/... verified) but not for the architect.
- Post-resolution writes into any opened project: .swarm/{bundled-skills(41 skills, 1.2 MB), config.example.json, advisories/, evidence/, knowledge-events.jsonl, knowledge-receipts-v2.jsonl(+snapshot), learning-health.json, locks/, repo-graph.json(+fingerprint), telemetry.jsonl} = 1.3 MB, plus '.swarm/' appended to .git/info/exclude so git status stays clean.

### Hot-path latency (`perf`)

On a fast Linux/tmpfs host with warm git, one architect turn with 5 tool calls costs ~1.99 s of plugin latency before the provider is called (system.transform 444 ms + messages.transform 443 ms + 5 x (before 92 ms + after 128 ms), Node p50, results/node-hooks.json). CPU profiles show almost no plugin self time on those paths: 84-90 % of the wall clock is deliberate setTimeout sleeping. readSwarmFileAsync (src/hooks/utils.ts:287-341) treats ENOENT as a retryable race and sleeps 4 x 10 ms per MISSING .swarm file, and readCachedParsedFile/readCachedTextFile short-circuit before the cache when the file is absent (swarm-artifact-cache.ts:176/242), so a project without .swarm artifacts re-pays 40 ms per missing-file read on every hook, forever: probe-timers counted 40 x 10 ms timers in one system.transform, and materializing the files drops system.transform 443->93, messages.transform 429->6, before 90->1.7, after 118->28 ms. Second contributor is 2 git subprocesses per architect tool.execute.after (15.3 ms/call, 13 %) from hive-promoter bypassing the cohort cache built to prevent exactly that (quantifies the already-confirmed KNOWLEDGE-1). Third is validateSwarmPath, a synchronous lstat+realpath+existsSync walk re-run inside the retry loop, producing 246-484 blocking sync fs calls per single hook invocation. Init: repro-704's 400 ms deadline times server() only (123 ms Node), while the 8.5 MB bundle import it excludes costs 1029 ms; 68 % of server() is 5 git subprocesses whose own budget is 3000 ms. Growth is mostly bounded (telemetry rotates, receipts plateau) except .swarm/runs/<sid>/memory.jsonl, appended every messages.transform for a feature disabled by default.

Contracts observed:

- Hook surface returned by server(): chat.message, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.chat.messages.transform, tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, event, command.execute.before, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete, config, agent, automation, tool (129 entries) — identical under Node 22 and Bun 1.3.11 (results/boot-*.jsonl).
- messages.transform and system.transform are composeHandlers chains run sequentially (src/index.ts:3386 and :3510); safeHook wraps each handler for errors only — there is no per-hook latency budget anywhere in the plugin.
- messages.transform latency is INDEPENDENT of conversation length: 439.0 / 444.9 / 442.6 ms p50 at 20 / 100 / 400 messages (results/node-hooks.json). The per-turn cost is fixed overhead, not message replay.
- Child (coder) sessions are cheap: the same before+after pair costs 2.35-2.86 ms p50 vs 92+128 ms on the architect session. Every finding below is architect-path cost.
- Per-turn .swarm write set for one messages.transform (default config, 286 write syscalls): knowledge-events.jsonl +1754 B, knowledge-receipts-v2.jsonl +987 B, knowledge-receipts-v2.snapshot.json rewritten +768 B, telemetry.jsonl +854 B (rotated), runs/<sid>/memory.jsonl +208 B (not rotated).

Coverage gaps:

- No Windows or macOS measurement at all. Every subprocess, cold-filesystem and AV-scan number here is a best case; PERF-1, PERF-4, PERF-6, PERF-7 and PERF-11 all get worse on Windows, and the AGENTS.md invariant-1 deadline is enforced per platform.
- Hooks were driven directly from dist/index.js with a stub ctx.client, not inside a real OpenCode host. Whether OpenCode awaits these transforms serially before dispatching the provider call is assumed from the v1 plugin contract, not observed — if the host overlapped them, the per-turn totals would shrink.
- The project under test is 30 files (400 for probe-lag.mjs). A monorepo changes repo-graph build time, git ls-files/check-ignore cost and the number of .swarm artifacts that exist.
- Ledger-replay slope is UNKNOWN, not zero: knowledge-receipts-v2.jsonl plateaued at ~6.6 KB over 300 cycles because the synthetic messages repeat and dedup, so a session with genuinely distinct receipts was never simulated. PERF-12 is reported as a lock/IO cost, not a growth cost, for that reason.
- Only the five per-turn hooks plus event were timed. experimental.session.compacting, command.execute.before, experimental.text.complete, config and agent were not measured, and none of the 129 tool executors were timed individually — 'the largest tools' in the lane brief is not covered.
- tool before+after (read, coder child session) shows p50 2.35 ms but p95 219.5 ms (Node) / 247.4 ms (Bun) — a ~100x tail that was not root-caused. First-call toolchain probes (PERF-11) and proper-lockfile contention (PERF-12) are both plausible and were not separated.
- The RSS slope in PERF-13 was measured over 300 cycles only and no retainer was identified; it may be allocator slack.
- The DEBUG_SWARM / OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG code paths were explicitly disabled in every harness, so the cost of the debug-gated console.error diagnostics on the hot path is unmeasured.
- Config variation was not swept: everything was measured with no config file (schema defaults). knowledge.enabled=false, hive_enabled=false, repo_graph.enabled=false and turbo/full-auto modes would each change the measured per-turn cost substantially and none were run.

### Windows / Node portability census (`portability`)

878 runtime files censused (5927 raw hits, 33 rules); every high-signal class read at the hit. Bun-only API (class 10) and AbortSignal.timeout (class 5) are clean and statically guarded; import.meta.url-derived paths (class 9) hold under the npm plugin cache. Material findings: (1) six Windows sites hand a .cmd/.bat shim or bare npm to a shell-less spawn (test_runner vitest/jest/mocha, incremental-verify, directive predicates, PHP, pkg-audit) which Node>=20.12 (EINVAL) and Bun.spawn cannot execute; (2) 17 containment checks compare JS-realpathSync paths case-sensitively on Windows; (3) the bunSpawn Node fallback defaults stdin to pipe and 11 call sites omit stdin / 19 omit timeout (Desktop Node sidecar hang class); (4) four direct child_process sites lack timeout/stdin bounds; plus low-severity CRLF, rmSync-without-maxRetries, mixed-separator, cmd /c quoting, and env-scrub items. Coverage: PR CI is ubuntu-only unless the diff touches 8 whitelisted dirs; no test executes a .cmd shim; Node-sidecar smoke is merge-queue-only.

### Repo graph and language backends (`repograph`)

Wiring is complete (export -> tool-metadata -> AGENT_TOOL_MAP incl. explorer/coder -> prompts -> docs/tests) and init honours invariant 1 via the post-resolution queue. The defects are cost and staleness contracts, measured on this checkout (4,152 nodes): (1) toolAfter awaits the startup build BEFORE its write-tool filter and the scan phase has no wall-clock budget - 265 s here - so every tool result stalls until the build ends; (2) the freshness stamp hashes package.json version, so every release (3-6/day) forces that full rebuild; (3) each write tool re-serializes a 37 MB pretty JSON graph plus a full fingerprint walk inside the awaited hook (~1.1 s) and the next turn re-parses/validates it synchronously (~0.5 s); (4) any workspace past max_files or the 5 s walk budget (easily hit on Windows) is permanently 'inconclusive' and never refreshed at startup. Also: docs still describe a regex-only, no-tree-sitter startup path; tree-sitter Query objects are recompiled per file and leaked; a sync builder stack and several exports have no caller; context_map's sole post-agent caller passes files_touched=[]; core tree-sitter.wasm is copy-pinned while web-tree-sitter floats on ^0.25.0.

### Adversarial security (threat model) (`security2`)

Repository content is the plugin's unguarded trust boundary. sanitizeContextText is the only injection filter on the architect-context path and it neutralises exactly five XML/markdown shapes -- plain-prose forged approvals, non-`system` open tags, and the ChatML/Llama/Human control vocabularies of the local models AGENTS.md invariant 10 targets all pass through byte-identical (demonstrated). Two surfaces skip it entirely: skill auto-injection (default ON) puts a repo SKILL.md `description:` frontmatter line at the TOP of a delegated subagent's prompt, and the opt-in context capsule pushes a repo file's first JSDoc block verbatim into output.system -- both demonstrated end-to-end with production functions. The shared command classifier is simultaneously over- and under-blocking: unanchored substring rules make `echo "graceful shutdown"`, `rg -n shutdown src/`, `git commit -m "...reboot..."` and `man shutdown` unwaivable CATASTROPHIC blocks for every agent by default, while `git -C . push --force` and `git push origin +main` are only 'unknown'. Protected-path case-folding is keyed to process.platform==='win32', so on macOS's case-insensitive default filesystem `.Swarm/plan.json` is allowed while `.swarm/plan.json` is denied. Full-Auto's phase-approval gate accepts an unsigned evidence file belonging to a different session. And a new member of the #1896 redirect-FP family: `bun test > /dev/null 2>&1` is hard-blocked as an out-of-workspace write.

Contracts observed:

- .swarm/curator-briefing.md, .swarm/context-map.json, .swarm/plan.json, .swarm/evidence/<phase>/full-auto-*.json are repo-resident inputs; `.git/info/exclude` does not untrack files a repository already commits (verified with a throwaway git repo)
- sanitizeContextText (src/hooks/context-sanitizer.ts:26) is the sole architect-context injection filter; blocks control/zero-width/BiDi chars, ```, `system:` line prefix, <system>/<tool_call> open tags, and ALL </tag> closing tags
- skillPropagation.enabled defaults to true (src/config/schema.ts:2240); injectSkillsIntoDelegation mutates args.prompt in place at src/index.ts:3799
- checkDestructiveCommand (tool-before.ts:358) runs for every bash/shell call from any agent when guardrails.block_destructive_commands !== false (schema default true) and throws on any classifier immediate-block rule before target-aware evaluation
- classifyCommandRisk (full-auto/policy.ts:401): catastrophic\|destructive -> deny, safe -> allow, everything else -> escalate_critic
- isPolicyProtectedPath / matchesAuthorityDenyPrefix case-fold only when the RUNTIME platform is win32 (protected-path-policy.ts:38-44, file-authority.ts:526-528)
- verifyFullAutoPhaseApproval (full-auto/phase-approval.ts:97) gates phase_complete on a plain JSON file matching {phase, trigger_source:'phase_boundary', verdict:'APPROVED'} within a 24h TTL
- Outbound HTTPS: registry.npmjs.org (version-check.ts:175), gitingest.com (gitingest.ts:37), api.tavily.com / api.search.brave.com (web-search-provider.ts:88,153), arbitrary URL (external-skill-discover.ts:37)

Coverage gaps:

- No OpenCode host, no macOS, no Windows: SEC2-6's filesystem behaviour (APFS case-insensitivity, NTFS trailing dot/space stripping) is documented OS semantics plus a demonstrated lexical result, not an observed write on those platforms. A reviewer with a macOS host should confirm the .Swarm/ write lands on .swarm/.
- No live model was run against any composed prompt. Every injection candidate (SEC2-1/2/3/9) proves the bytes reach the instruction channel; none proves the model obeys.
- src/sast/rules/* (10 files; javascript-call-classifier.ts is a 1390-line hand-rolled JS tokenizer) was only spot-checked — the oversized/malformed path fails safe to 'ambiguous' (line 1254). No FN/FP corpus was run over the SAST families, and the other 9 language rule files were not read.
- file-authority.ts's 8-step zone/prefix/glob evaluation order was read but not exercised as a matrix; getGlobMatcher's malformed-pattern catch branch is unreachable (picomatch tolerates '[', '{a', '!(', '+(a\|', '[a-' without throwing), so its 'permissive matcher' comment vs `() => false` body is inert and not reported.
- Memory recall (src/memory/prompt-block.ts) uses redactSecrets + an explicit untrusted header + the unforgeable bundle_ anchor, and is opt-in; I did not attempt to forge a bundle marker or test the write-time sentinel ban end-to-end.
- Windows native sandbox runner protocol and capability-probe identity strings were not examined (carried over from the first security lane).
- The knowledge-injector hook itself was not driven end-to-end (its gate needs a live session + knowledge store); SEC2-1 exercises the exact sanitize+compose expressions at knowledge-injector.ts:1247-1256 rather than the surrounding hook.
- Whether a repository realistically ships `.swarm/**` is a judgement call: I proved git tracks it across `.git/info/exclude`, but did not survey real consumer repos for committed `.swarm` directories.

### .swarm write-path census (`state`)

The .swarm/ surface is unusually well governed - 106 registry rows, a coverage ratchet, an atomic-write grammar registry, a temp-residue quarantine, and close archive/clean lists - and both retention gates pass on this checkout. The defects are at the seams. The most serious is not under .swarm/ at all: the default worktree base resolves to <project-parent>/.swarm-worktrees (src/worktree/core.ts:583), so every sibling checkout shares one directory, while plugin-init orphan recovery and /swarm reset-session decide what to delete there using only the current project's ownership records - the first force-rm's other projects' live lane worktrees, the second rm -rf's the whole shared tree. The governance layer has four structural blind spots: it is module-granular not stream-granular (.swarm/advisories/), its writer regexes ignore mkdir/copy/rename/delete (the unbounded home-level embeddings model cache), it scans src/ only so agent-written .swarm/outputs, .swarm/loop and .swarm/review-v8 trees are invisible and never cleaned, and its doc-to-data contract is row-id presence only, which is how a row for the nonexistent .swarm/handoff-continuation.json survives. Two registry rows also assert atomicity their writers do not have (skill-changelog trim and evidence trajectory truncation are unlocked in-place rewrites). Invariant 8 is in good shape - nearly every module-level session map has an explicit cap - with the real cross-session exposure being the unscoped process-global event bus rather than the maps.

Contracts observed:

- Runtime state lives only under the project root .swarm/, reached via ctx.directory and validateSwarmPath (src/hooks/utils.ts:157); process.cwd() is a documented direct-CLI/test fallback only (AGENTS.md invariant 4).
- Every durable-writing module under src/ must appear in RETENTION_REGISTRY.writerModules or EXEMPT_WRITER_MODULES; enforced by scripts/check-retention-registry.ts (issue #2036). Coverage is per MODULE, not per stream, and the writer detector is 18 content-write/SQLite-open regexes (:62-81).
- Production atomic writes under .swarm/ go through atomicWriteSwarmFile (containment, <target>.<hex32>.tmp grammar, fsync, bounded rename retry over EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES/EEXIST, exact own-temp cleanup); every other temp grammar must be registered in SWARM_TEMP_GRAMMARS with a WRITER_CLASSIFICATION entry (issue #2035).
- /swarm close is the retention boundary: ARCHIVE_ARTIFACTS (34 files, close.ts:400), ACTIVE_STATE_TO_CLEAN (21 files, :518), ACTIVE_STATE_DIRS_TO_CLEAN (8 dirs, :613), with TERMINAL_STATE_FILES removed unconditionally even when archiving failed (:561).
- Anything session-scoped is keyed by sessionID and every module-level map needs an explicit eviction strategy (AGENTS.md invariant 8); the repo's idioms are capSessionMap (src/index.ts:278) and MAX_* + FIFO evictors.
- docs/observability-retention-registry.md claims to cover 'every durable stream under .swarm/ and the platform-data roots', but states its own doc-to-data contract is row-id presence, not table-cell equality (:22-26).

Coverage gaps:

- No Windows or macOS host was available: every portability claim (STATE-10 rename retry, STATE-11 reserved device names and trailing-dot collapse, STATE-14 case-insensitive db keys, STATE-18 darwin config==data) is derived from source and Win32/HFS+ semantics, not executed. A reviewer with a Windows runner should confirm STATE-11 by attempting mkdir .swarm\\evidence\\con.
- STATE-1 and STATE-2 were confirmed statically plus by evaluating resolveWorktreeBaseDir on two sibling paths; the end-to-end deletion was NOT executed (it is destructive and the checkout is read-only). The exact behaviour of `git -C repoA worktree remove <repoB worktree>` was reasoned from removeWorktree's code path (src/worktree/core.ts:1059-1118), not run.
- STATE-12's cross-project write was reasoned from the unscoped singleton; it was not reproduced with two live plugin instances in one process, and I did not establish how often OpenCode actually loads the plugin twice in one host process (Desktop multi-project behaviour is unverified).
- Retention behaviour of the 27 fix-in-issue rows (issue #2309: summaries/, capsules/, runs/, lane-results/, evolution/, review-receipts/, doc-drift-phase-N.json and 15 more that accumulate across sessions) was read but deliberately NOT filed as candidates - the repo already owns them with dated dispositions. If the audit wants those re-litigated, that is a separate pass.
- SQLite-side state (swarm.db schema/migration behaviour, memory.db, repo-memory.sqlite, WAL sidecar handling at close) was only surveyed at the path level; no migration replay or corruption test was run.
- Migration paths for older layouts were spot-checked only where close touches them (SWARM_PLAN in all three legacy locations is correctly cleaned, close.ts:1966-1971). The .knowledge-migrated / .knowledge-external-migrated sentinels and src/memory/jsonl-migration.ts were not traced end to end.
- Lock correctness was not audited: proper-lockfile usage, the .swarm/locks/ stale-break windows, and the wx-existence locks in prm/trajectory-store.ts and parallel/file-locks.ts were read for path inventory only, not for liveness or fairness.
- The census's readers heuristic is basename-based; I re-verified by hand only the paths I filed on. Other entries in census.json's pathsWithNoReaderFound list may still be genuine dead state and were not individually chased.

### Tests and CI (`testsci`)

3,078 test files (~1.09M lines, 2.4:1 vs 450K src; 499 over the 500-line cap) run per-file in a 6-shard round-robin (498 files/cell; ci.yml comments say ~278). PR tier is ubuntu-only unless detect-paths matches a prefix list that omits src/utils, src/db, src/git, src/cli, src/hooks, src/config; integration, coverage, smoke (Node-sidecar repro-704/1873), PHP, Rust run only in merge_group. Live MG runs take 31-65 min (Windows cells 16-23 min + up to 21 min runner queue, then serialized unit->integration->smoke). Flake detection fires (verified live) but is advisory and sees only failed MG runs; quarantined files never execute on their OS so cannot 'prove out'. Coverage counts only loaded files and includes tests/helpers. Line-scoped lints ignore comments; invariant-3 timeout check is advisory-only; two release-fragment gates contradict; docs cite missing test paths; tests/ and scripts/ are never type-checked.

Contracts observed:

- bunfig.toml [test] preload: prod-store-tripwire.ts + executable-resolver-pin.ts; coverageDir ./coverage; no coverageSkipTestFiles
- scripts/ci/quarantined-tests{,-macos,-windows,-integration}.txt subtracted (comm -23) before sharding; per-OS lists on that OS only
- Unit set: find src tests/unit tests/adversarial tests/architect tests/cli tests/tools tests/helpers tests(maxdepth1) '*.test.ts'
- scripts/ci/run-test-with-timeout.ts: bun --smol --preload bun-32056-keepalive.ts, --kill-timeout 180, exit 124; local mirror bun run test:unit:ci
- Escape hatches: MOCK_ALLOWLIST_ENFORCE, TEST_CAP_ENFORCE, FRAGMENT_CHECK_ENFORCE, DRIFT_CHECK_ENFORCE(repo var), *_USAGE_ENFORCE, ERROR_CHANNEL_DISCARD_ENFORCE, SKILL_ASSERTIONS_STRICT, SWARM_ALLOW_FULL_SUITE
- COVERAGE_THRESHOLD 65.00, COVERAGE_SHARD_INDEX/COUNT 6 -> merge-lcov.mjs; flake-annotations-*-shard-N -> flake-detection.yml -> detect-and-quarantine-flakes.sh -> flake-suggestions + gh issue
- detect-paths 3-OS prefixes: src/worktree/ src/turbo/ src/sandbox/ src/plan/ src/parallel/ src/knowledge/ src/memory/ src/tools/ scripts/ .github/workflows/; Bun 1.3.13 in CI

Coverage gaps:

- Not read in full: check-event-contract/retention-registry/registry-citations/runtime-src-refs/skill-assertions bodies (~3.9K lines); ci-workflow-security.test.ts scans only ci.yml.
- 98 prompt-prose-asserting test files counted, not sampled; no integration/security/smoke file executed; run-test-with-timeout.ts not exercised on Windows/macOS (host Linux, Bun 1.3.11 vs CI 1.3.13).
