### Tool registry and agent tool maps (`tools`)

Registry mechanics are sound: 129 tools in TOOL_METADATA, compile-exhaustive TOOL_MANIFEST, single buildPluginToolObject, hard CI parity script, every tool exported/registered/mapped, multi-swarm prefixed tests exist, zod pairing OK on the current host. The load-bearing problems are semantic: (1) the per-agent allow-list is emitted as {tool:true} only, which under OpenCode's tools/permission semantics denies nothing — 'architect-only' is unenforced for ~117/129 tools and every agent likely carries all ~171 KB of tool schemas per turn; (2) tool_filter.overrides '[] denies all' is false; (3) knowledge.enabled=false unregisters 6 tools that agent maps and the architect prompt still grant and mandate; (4) getAgentConfigs fire-and-forget writes a new .swarm/evidence/agent-tools-init-<ts>.json per init with no root check or retention; (5) /swarm doctor tools is a tautology blind to config-dependent registration; (6) web_search is default-granted to sme/researcher but hard-fails without council.general; plus two untested bindings and working_directory policy divergence.

Contracts observed:

- TOOL_METADATA keys (src/tools/tool-metadata.ts) = TOOL_NAMES = plugin tool object keys (minus 6 knowledge_* when knowledge.enabled=false); AGENT_TOOL_MAP = exact inversion of TOOL_METADATA[*].agents; opt-in maps in constants.ts merged in getAgentConfigs by memory/external_skills/council/council.general/turbo/skills gates
- sdkConfig.tools = {allowed:true} + definition false flags only (agents/index.ts:1422-1441). Host: true≡{'*':'allow'}, false≡{'*':'deny'}, unlisted included; args converted via z.toJSONSchema({io:'input'}); plugin 1.18.3 tool() is identity; zod 4.3.6 inlined in dist
- createSwarmTool: directory = ctx.directory ?? process.cwd(); working_directory override only with allowWorkingDirectoryOverride → resolveWorkingDirectory + assertProjectRoot
- Writes .swarm/evidence/agent-tools-<sessionId\|init-<ts>>.json (agents/index.ts:1451-1472), read by src/services/diagnose-service.ts:1258; CI scripts/check-tool-registration.ts hard-fails (ci.yml:186)

Coverage gaps:

- OpenCode host semantics confirmed from docs (agents.mdx) and v1.18.3 tool/registry.ts; session/tools.ts resolve at the pinned tag was not fully quoted — reviewer should confirm no allow-list filter exists there.
- INFO (by design): 30/129 tools are reachable only via gates defaulting off — memory(3), council(4), general council(3 incl. web_fetch), turbo(6), skills(7), external skills(7); skill_generate/list/inspect/improve reach only skill_improver whose quota is gated by skill_improver.enabled (schema.ts:2309, default false). README lists lean_turbo_*/skill_* without the gate.
- INFO (verified OK): dist inlines zod 4.3.6, batch_symbols uses SDK's nested 4.1.8 via tool.schema, swarm_memory_outcome.anchors (line 62) holds a transform that fails z.toJSONSchema under default io:'output'; safe only because the host detects '_zod' structurally and converts with io:'input'.
- Caller-identity checks counted by grep (12/129 reference ctx.agent); per-tool audit outstanding. tests/unit/config: read agent-tool-map, constants, skill-tool-gating, tool-filter-council-hardening, memory-tool-gating only. Byte figures computed from schemas, not observed on the wire.
- Cross-scope: swarm_command default-granted to 12 agents incl. subagents (commands lane); extract_code_blocks in WRITE_TOOL_NAMES yet granted to docs/docs_design/designer/spec_writer (hooks lane); receipt-demanding hooks when knowledge disabled (hooks lane); council_*/curator_consolidation have zero swarm tools (agents lane); docs/configuration.md has a one-line tool_filter entry only (docs lane).

### End-to-end wiring census (`wiring`)

Script-driven census of every export -> plugin registration -> tool/agent map -> help/docs -> test chain in the plugin. The registration machinery the repo actually guards is clean: 129/129 tools are exported, registered, in TOOL_NAMES and in a map (check-tool-registration passes); 154/154 commands have handler+description+COMMAND_NAMES; 41 bundled skills == 41 package.json#files == 41 .opencode dirs; all 26 agents have a registration test. The gaps are exactly where no check script looks. (1) 111 of 6502 exported declarations in src/** are referenced nowhere at all - including a whole dead public API on src/evidence/gate-bridge.ts, three config-default constants that shadow live zod defaults, a DEFAULT_REQUIRED_GATES that contradicts the schema default, three test-only seams no test uses, and resetTrajectoryStep whose docblock claims it is called on session start; only 1 of the 111 was already filed by any sibling lane. A further 1097 are exported but used only inside their own file. (2) PrReviewDimensionTerminalState is an exported status union with zero references anywhere - its COVERED member exists only in the declaration. (3) 3 of the 11 registered hook keys (command.execute.before, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.text.complete) are never exercised through the object the plugin entry returns, only via directly-imported handlers - the exact class AGENTS.md invariant 10 says was dead for years. (4) The returned object carries an `automation` key that is not a Hooks member and has no reader, while `dispose` - a real Hooks key - is unregistered and cleanup rides on process.on('exit'). (5) 8 DEFAULT_MODELS entries are never consulted by agent registration (critic variants use getModel('critic'), curators use getModel('explorer')), so the registered model and the model that delegation preflight, cost accounting and the generated .swarm/config.example.json compute disagree. (6) curator_consolidation is registered by default with an empty AGENT_TOOL_MAP entry and no warning fires because [] is truthy. (7) 19 tools appear in no README or docs/*.md, only release-note fragments.

Contracts observed:

- Tools: TOOL_METADATA (129 keys) == TOOL_MANIFEST == buildPluginToolObject({}) == TOOL_NAMES/TOOL_NAME_SET; AGENT_TOOL_MAP is the exact inversion of TOOL_METADATA[*].agents; 7 opt-in maps in src/config/constants.ts (MEMORY/EXTERNAL_SKILL/COUNCIL/GENERAL_COUNCIL/TURBO/SKILL/PR_REVIEW_CHILD) are merged conditionally in getAgentConfigs; 3 @tool-opt-out bindings are documented seams. Enforced by scripts/check-tool-registration.ts (hard-fail in CI) and re-used by scripts/drift-check.ts.
- Agents: ALL_AGENT_NAMES = 26; createAgents({}) registers 21 (docs_design/designer/council_* are opt-in); architect is the only primary and has its model deleted; every subagent model comes from getModelForAgent -> DEFAULT_MODELS[baseAgentName] ?? DEFAULT_MODELS.default, EXCEPT the 6 critic variants (getModel('critic')) and the 4 curators (getModel('explorer')).
- Hooks: @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.3 declares 21 Hooks keys (node_modules/@opencode-ai/plugin/dist/index.d.ts:173-315). src/index.ts returns 11 of them plus name/agent/automation, which are not Hooks members.
- Commands: COMMAND_REGISTRY (154) is the single source of truth for VALID_COMMANDS, COMMAND_NAMES, the architect SLASH COMMANDS block (buildSlashCommandsList), and the swarm_command tool policy sets; alias + toolPolicy validation runs at module load.
- Skills: BUNDLED_PROJECT_SKILLS (41) == package.json#files skill entries (41) == .opencode/skills dirs; materialization target is .swarm/bundled-skills only; mirror pairs classified in src/config/skill-mirrors.ts and checked by bun run drift:check.

Coverage gaps:

- Enum census scoped to 20 named families / 106 members (plan task+phase+migration status, evidence type+verdict, dispatch-lane status, background-delegation status, PR-workflow completion status, PR-feedback gate phase + publication generation state + push-attempt outcome, PR-review dimension terminal state + coverage kind + report verdict, worker status, PR-subscription status, PR-review circuit state, sandbox status, trace status, skill-usage pending state). The repo declares 70+ further union types matching /^export type \w*(Status\|Phase\|Verdict\|State\|Outcome\|Kind\|Transition\|Disposition\|Reason)/ in src (see the grep in scratchpad/wiring/); those were NOT member-level censused. Telemetry kinds were deliberately excluded (already reported).
- The producer/consumer classifier in wiring/enum-census.ts is a line-level regex heuristic and produced several false one-sided counts (?? fallbacks, table lookups, `case` on a mapped variable). Every flagged member was read in source before reporting, so no false positive was filed - but the converse is not proven: a member whose only 'producer' is a comment-adjacent line could be counted as produced. A reviewer wanting certainty should re-derive per-member producers with an AST pass, not the regex.
- Dead/over-export detection is a whole-word token index over identifiers in src, tests, test, scripts, examples, runners and evaluation-fixtures. It cannot see a symbol reached only via a computed member access (obj['some' + 'Name']), a re-export from dist consumed by an external package, or a name that appears in a .md/.json fixture but not in .ts. It also does not read node_modules, so a symbol imported only by an external consumer of the published package would be misclassified as dead. Each of the 28 rows quoted in WIRING-1 was individually re-verified with a full grep across src/tests/test/scripts/docs/README (exactly 1 hit each), but the remaining 83 dead rows in scratchpad/wiring/orphan-dead.txt were not individually re-verified.
- The declaration regex (^export (type\|interface\|const\|function\|class\|enum\|async function) NAME) matches lines inside template literals - e.g. `export function LoginForm(` inside a prompt example in src/agents/designer.ts:107 was matched. Such rows are excluded from the reported evidence but may remain in the raw counts (6502 / 1097); the 111-row dead list was inspected and contains no template-literal artefact.
- Hook entry-object test coverage is measured by string search for the key literal within the set of test files that call .server(...) or bootKnowledgeHost(...). A test that boots the entry and reaches a hook through an indirection (a helper that destructures it, a loop over Object.entries) would be missed. The three keys reported as untested were additionally hand-checked against every such file.
- No hook was invoked at runtime through the entry object as part of this audit - the plugin was not booted. WIRING-3 is a test-coverage claim, not a claim that the three hooks are broken.
- Command coverage checked docs by the literal '/swarm <name>' form; commands documented only by a pipe-separated family line (e.g. README.md:648 '/swarm skill-opt plan\|run\|status\|diff\|approve\|reject\|rollback\|history') were initially false-flagged and were removed after reading. Other such families may exist and would have been silently accepted, so the command-docs column is a floor.
- Skill wiring relies on bun run drift:check for the mirror and bundling contracts rather than an independent re-derivation; drift:check currently reports no skill drift. Per-skill prompt-reachability (does any agent prompt or MODE stub actually load each of the 41 bundled skills) was not enumerated.
- Runtime tool-permission semantics (whether {tool:true} actually restricts under the host) were taken from the tools lane and not re-derived here; this lane's 'default-agent reachable' column measures map membership, not enforced access.
- package.json#files was compared to BUNDLED_PROJECT_SKILLS only for skill entries; the rest of the packed-tarball surface was not audited (scripts/package-smoke.mjs and the package-check CI job own that).

## 5. Gap analysis against a first-class OpenCode plugin

Each row states what a first-class OpenCode plugin needs, what this one does, and what closing the gap
requires. Every "observed" cell is drawn from a finding that cleared the reviewer gate, and the
high-severity ones cleared a critic as well.

| Dimension | Observed | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Host contract, message channel | The host's converter has branches for user and assistant and no else, and its message type has no system member. The plugin splices synthetic system-role messages at fourteen sites in the hook and entry modules, and at a fifteenth in the memory injector, and records them delivered by checking its own output array. One site uses a flat shape with no parts array, which the converter dereferences unconditionally, so that turn throws rather than dropping. | Move every model-directed injection to the system-prompt surface the host renders. Assert delivery against a rendered role, not against the plugin's own insertion. Add a contract test that runs the host's real converter over the plugin's real output. |
| Host contract, tool identity | The host's task tool id is lowercase. Two gates compare against a capitalised literal, so the delegation loop detector never fires and the per-role model fallback never registers a route. A second, independent blocker sits behind the same failover: the error-signal extractor never descends into the field where every real provider error carries its text. | One case-insensitive normaliser for every tool-name comparison, and a test that loads the host's real tool ids rather than a fixture. Fix both failover blockers together or the failover stays dead. |
| Host contract, permission | The host runs no implicit permission check. Its own write tools call the permission bridge; the plugin's file-mutating tool never does, and the host keys permission hiding on a tool's own name, so a user's edit policy is inert for the coder's own write path. | Call the host-supplied permission bridge from every mutating tool, or register those tools under names the host's edit policy covers. |
| Host contract, cancellation | The host's session cancel does not cascade to child sessions, which is why its own child-session tool cancels explicitly. The lane dispatcher creates child sessions and never reads the host's abort signal. Four of 165 tool files read it. | Link the host abort signal to every created lane session and to long-running tool work. |
| Per-agent restriction | An agent's tool map is never read at all for a plugin-injected agent, because the host's only reader runs at config-file decode, before plugins load; for an agent authored in a configuration file it becomes permission rules where an allow is a no-op and only an explicit deny hides a tool. Across 21 agents, 2,388 intended denies over the plugin's own tool set are enforced zero times (2,745 over a 146-tool universe, of which the 21 the host does enforce come from its own defaults), and all 129 tools reach every agent. One agent that allow-lists nothing still receives 129. | Emit a per-agent `permission` block, the one field the host's agent merge copies, ordered last with a trailing deny-all and explicit allows. Writing explicit denies into the `tools` map would not work: for a plugin-injected agent an explicit `false` is as inert as a `true`. The host's tool-definition hook is not a lever here either — it receives only a tool id, so it can neither vary by agent nor remove a tool. |
| Per-turn cost | Every agent receives all 129 tool definitions on every agentic step: 169,124 characters, roughly 42,000 tokens, against 15,073 characters for the host's entire built-in tool set. The architect's system prompt is 8.9 times the host's largest. | A measured per-role budget and session-guarded injections. Schema trimming per agent is not available at the pinned host version, whose tool-definition hook is passed only a tool id; the levers that remain are the permission block and a smaller registry. |
| Lifecycle | The plugin registers no dispose hook although the host calls one on instance disposal. Module-level singletons hold telemetry, warnings, agent registries, clients and database handles; the telemetry writer pins the first project directory for the process; the project-database map has no eviction and grows three file descriptors per distinct root. | A per-instance container keyed by the project directory, a dispose hook that tears down that instance's workers, and an explicit eviction strategy on every module-level map. |
| Subprocess contract | The Node fallback attaches its output listeners lazily, so any read issued after a process exits never settles and the bytes are already discarded. Eighteen call sites do exactly that, eleven on the success path. Init orphan recovery is inert on every Node host in a git repository; both worktree helpers never settle; one path has no outer timeout at all. | Attach collectors eagerly at spawn. Add the read-after-exit case to the test suite, which today runs only under the other runtime, and run the portability smokes on pull requests rather than only in the merge queue. |
| Durable state ownership | The worktree base defaults to the project's parent, shared by every sibling checkout. Opening a second project force-deletes the first's in-flight lanes after git itself refuses the removal, and the session-reset command removes the shared base outright while its help text promises it deletes only one state file. The ownership primitive already exists in the codebase and is called from neither path. | Namespace the base per repository, prove ownership before any deletion, treat git's refusal as the not-ours signal rather than a reason to force, and require confirmation for a command that reaches outside the project root. |
| Gate satisfiability | Several default-on gates cannot be satisfied. A repair tool writes a sentinel requirement no code can ever record. A coverage gate reads an evidence entry type no producer writes. A phase gate reads a verdict field nothing assigns, whose only writer has test callers alone. A quality gate compares absolute totals against delta-sized thresholds and fails on any ordinary file. | A satisfiability lint: every gate that requires evidence must have a reachable producer, checked in CI. This is the single check that would have caught four separate blockers. |
| Denial ergonomics | Fewer than one denial site in ten names a concrete next action. The escalation circuit keys on a message's pre-colon prefix, so 391 distinct causes share one bucket while one cause fragments across five, and the ladder resets on every user prompt. The dry-run command that would explain a denial disagrees with the live gate on four of four commands tried. | One structured denial envelope carrying cause, observation and next call; a cause key independent of prose; a ladder that survives a turn boundary; and a dry-run that runs the same chain the gate runs. |
| Command classification | Five unanchored substring rules hard-block 16 of 23 ordinary developer commands as catastrophic, including a commit whose message mentions a shutdown handler and a grep for a SQL keyword, while a real namespaced delete passes. A redirect to the null device is treated as an out-of-workspace write. A flag whose purpose is to make force-pushing safer is blocked as catastrophic. | Anchor the rules, apply the null-device filter at the one call site that omits it, and add false-positive cases to the classifier's tests, which today contain none. |
| Portability | The Windows sandbox binary is absent from the package. Command shims are resolved with a Windows extension and then handed to a shell-free spawn, which cannot execute them; the correct wrapper exists in one module and is called by nothing else. Protected-path case folding keys off one platform and inverts for two entries, leaving them unprotected there. | Ship or build the runner, route every resolved shim through the existing wrapper, and run the portability-sensitive directories on Windows and macOS at pull-request time. |
| First-run path | The installer can destroy a configuration file it cannot parse. Documentation names a package that does not exist. The architect is not auto-selected, and its configured model is stripped while the diagnostic command echoes it back as if applied. Defaults resolve to a paid model for nine roles and a deprecated one for the coder, under a README that advertises a free tier. | An idempotent, non-destructive installer; verified runbooks; defaults that resolve without a paid or deprecated model; and diagnostics that report what the host actually received. |
| Observability | Most telemetry kinds have no consumer. The disable latch is invisible. Thirty-eight signals the code marks must-see go only to the host process's stderr, while the host's own logging endpoint is reachable and unused. Deferred warnings surface only through a diagnostic command that re-triggers them and mislabels them as init-time. | Use the host's logging endpoint for must-see signals, surface degraded states visibly, and stop re-entering the config loader inside the diagnostic path. |
| Retention and cleanup | Three plugin-caused state trees are absent from all 106 registry rows and survive session close, because the ratchet walks only the source directory and cannot see agent-written state. One authorization grant has no producer or consumer anywhere. A hundred and ten registry citations point at wrong lines, frozen in a shrink-only baseline. | Extend the ratchet to cover streams rather than only writers, register the agent-written trees, and retire the citation baseline rather than freezing it. |
| Test and CI hygiene | Three test directories fail deterministically as batches and pass file by file, while the testing guide lists two of them as batch-safe and contradicts itself four lines apart. A compliance checker emits 253 unfollowable annotations on every pull request against a CI structure that no longer exists, and exits zero. No test asserts any denial's recovery clause on text the model actually receives. | Fix the mock leakage or stop documenting those directories as batch-safe, rebuild the checker against the real workflow, and add a ratchet that pins recovery clauses on the live channel. |
| Process | Seven months produced 690 analysed releases of a 50 MB package, 211 bug-fix sections against 81 feature sections in the last 247 releases, and fix-of-fix chains spanning five to nine versions. Of 126 pull requests read in depth, 34 merged with no independent reviewer, and model-authored verdicts posted from the maintainer account counted as approval. A stale bot closes labelled defects after 37 days. | Batched releases, pruning of the pending fragments, independent review by a different model family plus a human for high findings, and stale exemptions for defects. |
| Roadmap coverage | The open-issue set was replaced wholesale during this audit. The bookkeeping is sound, but the roadmap was built from the previous issue set rather than from the codebase, so it inherited that set's blind spots. Two issues by the same author 55 seconds apart take opposite positions on the same code. Several bullets propose work already merged. The one critical finding the tracker did own was retired five minutes after its replacement was filed, and the replacement drops the change that would make its own exit gate reachable. | Rebuild the roadmap from verified defects rather than from the prior issue set, reconcile the two contradictory issues before either closes, and strike the already-shipped bullets so sequencing reflects real work. |

Critic batches: 15 decision files covering 45 findings. Reviewer-confirmed HIGH/CRITICAL findings without a critic decision: 0.

What the critic gate changed: of 45 decisions, 30 upheld the reviewer, 15 lowered the severity and 0 overturned the finding outright. 44 were reached by running code rather than by reading it.

Read that zero carefully rather than as a boast. No critic rejected a finding outright, but one contradicted another: batch c14, deciding HOST-1, established that the mechanism batch c04 had upheld for TOOLS-1 is wrong for every agent this plugin ships, and said the two findings must be merged. Both are recorded UPHELD, so a decision that overturned a framing appears in this table as agreement. The refusals in this audit came from the reviewer gate, not this one — 15 candidates were disproved there, and none here. A critic gate with no refusals is worth less as evidence than its upheld count suggests, and the honest reading is that it corrected severities and mechanisms rather than rejecting findings.

## 7. The replacement roadmap, validated

On 2026-09-02 the repository's open-issue set was replaced. The roughly 97 issues that were open when this audit began were bulk-closed, each with a comment consolidating it into one of 44 newly created issues organised as Workstreams A through G with titles of the form "PR n of m". That work was done by a coordinated group of language models. This section is an independent validation of it: every issue was read, its factual claims about the codebase were checked against source, and its scope was compared against the findings verified above.

44 issues validated. Verdicts: MISDIAGNOSED 2, SOUND_WITH_CORRECTIONS 39, SOUND 3. 255 factual claims about the codebase were checked against source; 37 are false and 78 are only partly true.

Every root-cause diagnosis I could check held up — the pkg-audit mock.module self-delegation recursion is visible in the source (tests/unit/tools/pkg-audit-composer.test.ts:12 spreads realDiscovery then calls realDiscovery.isCommandAvailable from inside the replacement), the raw mkdtempSync/rmSync teardowns are real, #2455 and #2191/#2192 really are quarantine-only, and 2478 explicitly forbids blanket timeout inflation. Metadata plus a suppression-satisfiable soak gate is how a quarantine becomes permanent with paperwork.
- wsBC: Two verified CI gaps large enough to invalidate the workstream's own outcome statement are in no issue. First, 69 integration test cases (30 in tests/integration/lang/prompt-injection.test.ts, 39 in tool-profiles.test.ts) are executed by no CI job: .github/workflows/ci.yml:787 runs `find tests/integration test -maxdepth 1 -name '*.test.ts'`, which cannot reach the lang subdirectory. Second, TESTSCI-13's detect-release predicate at ci.yml:56 — `git log -1 --format='%B' \| grep -qE 'release-please--\|^chore\(main\): release'` — greps the merge-group HEAD's full message, which embeds the source branch and PR title, so an ordinary PR can be classified a release and every required check reports success with zero steps run. Workstream C is titled 'CI and test stability' and claims 'Drift, coverage gaps, and ratchet bypasses structurally cannot ship'; a job whose find misses a directory and a predicate that can green the entire required set are both larger bypasses than the three citation hatches the workstream does remove.

- wsD: The single highest-risk item is #2484 (D5, plan ledger). Four critic-upheld HIGH findings (PLAN-1, PLAN-2, PLAN-3, PLAN-4) sit in the plan subsystem, none appears anywhere in Workstream D, and all four are in the READER (src/plan/manager.ts loadPlan, src/tools/save-plan.ts, src/tools/get-approved-plan.ts) rather than in the storage substrate. Migrating the substrate first carries every one of them into the new store, and the issue's acceptance criterion — replay both backends, compare root hash and terminal projection — is structurally incapable of detecting any of them, because both backends would be equally wrong. - wsD: 'Hash parity' is not one property. src/plan/ledger.ts hosts two mutually incompatible plan-hash functions — computePlanHash (:431, status-inclusive) and computePlanStructureHash (:491, status-excluded) — and the snapshot payload_hash field holds output from either depending on who wrote it (takeSnapshotEvent defaults to the first at :1193; the plan-critic gate overrides to the second at delegation-gate.ts:1836 and :1940), while get_approved_plan always compares with the first (:233). Byte-exact preservation of that field is an instruction to preserve PLAN-3. Separately, the issue's 'hash-chain' language is wrong on its own terms: LedgerEvent has no prev-event-hash; computeLedgerEventHash is called at only two sites and only for the root event's epoch binding.

There are already two sites in tree — memory-family-migration.ts:320 (throws, breaking /swarm memory unlink always) and sqlite-provider.ts:2277 (optional-chained, silently reporting 0 rows). Two of my issues touch the same chain and must not add to it: 2488's shared task-ID resolver runs in micro-reflector on tool.execute.after (src/index.ts:4186 — Task-gated, so per-delegation not per-call, but #1606's explicit 'keep the resolver bounded and non-throwing in the tool-after path' constraint was dropped when the issue was rewritten), and the repo-graph incremental hook already runs on the same chain at src/index.ts:4415. Neither issue carries a per-call latency budget.
- wsE: Every issue that depends on the repo graph is written as if the graph is present. It frequently is not: repo_graph.enabled/init_refresh default true but the build runs off the post-resolution task queue after server() resolves (src/index.ts:1113), and this checkout — which has a populated .swarm/ from real plugin sessions — has no .swarm/repo-graph.json and no .swarm/cache/impact-map.json at all. So 2488's graph-first surfaces must render 'no graph yet' as a first-class state (the issue only mentions stale/low-confidence), and 2492's impact scope hits the cold, unbounded, synchronous analyzer walk as its DEFAULT path, not as the edge case the issue lists.
- wsE: Retrieval-quality proposals are not testable as written. 2490 asks in the same breath for injected embedding/reranker seams 'so tests avoid model downloads' AND a 'Paraphrase improvement' proof. With a fake provider, a paraphrase-recall delta measures the fixture, not the model — it proves the fusion plumbing and nothing about the quality claim in the issue's own title. Proving the quality claim needs the real ~25 MB MiniLM download (src/memory/embeddings/local-provider.ts:128), which the offline-first constraint rules out of CI. The issue must state per test which of the two it buys. By contrast the same issue's honest-degradation bullet IS crisply testable and is the batch's highest value-per-line item: src/utils/logger.ts:17 gates the 'falling back to lexical-only' warning behind OPENCODE_SWARM_DEBUG=1, so today a user who enables memory.embeddings and silently gets lexical-only retrieval is told nothing (audit KNOWLEDGE-13).
- wsE: The declared E1 -> E2 -> E3 chain is inverted where it matters. E1 wires the graph-first consumers; E2 builds the symbol-edge index caches those consumers need (src/tools/repo-graph/query.ts:525, :563, :961 are all still O(edges)/O(symbolEdges) per call). Landing E1 first ships a known per-query regression that E2 then repairs. E3's dependency on E2 meanwhile is spurious: nothing in src/memory reads the repo graph — the E3 title's 'graph-memory' conflates the #1223 memory-retrieval subsystem with the #1539 repo-graph KG capstone, which share no storage and no code path.

- wsE: The batch also inherits an undiagnosed delivery problem. 2491 builds on a routing signal delivered through pendingAdvisoryMessages in the experimental.chat.messages.transform chain (src/hooks/guardrails/messages-transform.ts:600-646), which unshifts a fresh {role:'system'} message when none exists — precisely the shape audit MAIN-10 (CRITICAL) and HOOKS-7 (HIGH, critic UPHELD) show the host drops before the request. So the current 'advisory-only' baseline may in fact be 'not delivered at all', and any enforcement design that leans on advisories will fail identically. 2488's graph-first blocks are safe here because system-enhancer rides experimental.chat.system.transform (src/index.ts:3510-3517), the surface the audit says is unaffected — that asymmetry should be stated in both issues.

'Diff-before-rewrite with backup' cannot detect the case because loadJson (src/cli/index.ts:269-283) returns null for both 'missing' and 'unparseable', and the Required-tests list has no unparseable-config case. The documented remedy loop is also untouched: docs/getting-started.md:130, :235 and README.md:253 all tell a user whose plugin will not load to re-run this exact installer.
- wsF1: Adjacent issues in the same workstream duplicate scope: 2493's 'CI check against native command collisions' and 2494's 'cross-host command/skill collision rules' are the same gate, one PR apart. Whichever lands second finds it written or writes a second one.
- wsF1: Two issues are gated on work that will rewrite what they touch, or on work whose own correctness is unproven. 2496 (a pure mechanical close.ts split, corresponding to no audit finding at all) is declared dependent on #2483, which will rewrite the very artifact tables and SQLite backup path being extracted — the split is cheapest before that migration. 2497 and 2498 both build headless execution on gates the audit reports as non-functional by default: EVIDENCE-2 (req_coverage's only input has no producer, so the #2242 preflight gate can never pass) and PRREVIEW-1 (Profile A lanes cannot settle on a default install, with PRREVIEW-8 recording that no test exercises the production settlement path).
- wsF2: Every issue in this batch is a one-paragraph re-statement of a large closed source issue (#1227, #1577, #1678, #1826, #1677). The load-bearing engineering content — the correctness gaps, the failure modes, the acceptance criteria — lives in the closed issue, not the open one. Validating any of them required reading the closed source; an implementer working from the roadmap issue alone would lose, for example, #1577's cross-artifact id contract (namespace-aware extraction is necessary but not sufficient), #1678's 'never a default flip' constraint, and #1826's entire Workstream A (sandbox_mode x approval_policy).
- wsF2: The roadmap's premises were frozen at each source issue's last triage, and several have since gone stale in BOTH directions. #1826's triage said 'none of the proposed concepts exist' — at HEAD src/harness, src/evaluation and a nine-subcommand /swarm skill-opt lifecycle exist, so F11 over-scopes. #1677's triage said 'design-rationale.md:310 does not exist — the file is only ~100 lines' — the file is 585 lines and :310 is exactly the quoted sentence, so F12 under-scopes. The issues instruct 're-anchor line citations before implementation'; the premises need re-anchoring too.
- wsF2: Four of the six issues rest on subsystems the audit found structurally broken, and none of them names the defect: F10 assumes PR lanes settle (PRREVIEW-1, CRITICAL, critic-upheld — re-derived here: the controller-bound child prompt renders mode/workflow_lane/pr_head_sha/revision_digest/assigned_item_ids but never batchId/laneId, which submit_pr_review_result requires); F9 assumes coverage scoring works (EVIDENCE-2 — no producer for diff/files_changed evidence, every FR 'missing'); F12's headline parallel flip assumes phases advance (PLAN-4 — no advancing writer, save_plan re-pins to phases[0]); F7/F8 assume 'existing containment' is a coherent reusable thing (PORT-002, PORT-010, EVIDENCE-3, TOOLS-9 say it is three different implementations).
- wsF2: Grepping all 44 open roadmap issue bodies shows the audit's highest-severity cross-cutting defects are unowned by the entire A-G programme: no issue mentions 'dispose' (MAIN-1/INIT-8 — no teardown, duplicated PR-monitor pollers, which F10's restart-mid-loop test depends on), none mentions role:'system' / messages.transform (MAIN-10 CRITICAL and HOOKS-7 — 14 synthetic system messages dropped (the validator wrote 17, a raw grep count later corrected by the report-level review) before the model, which F10's oversight guidance and F12's migration warnings both rely on), none mentions current_phase (PLAN-4), none mentions req_coverage or files_changed (EVIDENCE-2), none mentions tool_filter or allow-list semantics (TOOLS-1 — per-agent allow-lists are additive under host v1.18.3 [Corrected by the report-level critic: for a plugin-injected agent neither polarity survives, so a preset of tool defaults is a no-op in either direction until a permission block exists.], so any restricting default is a no-op).
- wsF2: The batch is back-loaded with capstones that each depend on a leg the roadmap has not proven: F10 needs A1's settlement repair (reachable only transitively via F6), F11 needs B2's Windows sandbox boundary (not listed) and #1826's own #1824 two-knob work (dropped), F12 needs PLAN-4 (unowned) and MAIN-4 (unowned). F12 is the only issue in the batch with no dependency section at all, despite #1677 explicitly saying 'Sequence last among the v8.0 epics'.
- wsF2: Two of the five source issues (#1577, #1677) carried the `Stale` label before the 2026-09-02 re-baseline closed them. Audit MAIN-8 records that stale.yml auto-closes any issue after 30d+7d with only 'pinned,security' exempt — so the re-baseline is partly a response to a tracker policy that was itself flagged as a defect, and the closure comments ('re-open only if that issue drops it from its acceptance gates') put the burden of noticing a dropped criterion on a future reader rather than on a gate.
- wsF2: Sizing is uniformly optimistic. Five of six cannot be one PR by their own scope text; #1577 says its two halves 'share no implementation surface', #1826 is PR 7 of a 7-PR series with five workstreams, and #1227 is explicitly phased with a phase-0 refactor the roadmap hands to a different, narrower issue (F5). Only F12, if held strictly to the frame (inventory + preset + migration + docs), is plausibly single-PR — and only if it does not have to fix the defects that make its flips meaningful.
- wsG: Four of the five issues assert a gap this repository has already closed, and none cites the in-repo mechanism it would duplicate. #2508's overlap detection exists (src/worktree/merge.ts:1769-1778, typed stage 'pre-merge-overlap'); #2508's purge preview exists (/swarm finalize --dry-run, src/commands/close.ts:2352-2356, documented as fully read-only); #2507's action-local 3-warn/5-stop circuit for `task` exists (src/hooks/gate-denial-tracker.ts:64-67, :96, backed by src/failures/action-circuit.ts with a /swarm guardrail-reset audited reset); #2506's 30-minute stale-lane settlement with a fail-open liveness probe exists for PR-workflow lanes (src/hooks/pr-workflow-gate.ts:2782, :2763-2770). The authors validated the ensemble side carefully - every ensemble default I checked matched the upstream source - and did not validate the opencode-swarm side at all. That asymmetry is the batch's defining defect.
- wsG: The batch repeatedly cites CLOSED issues as live failure modes: #2251 (closed-completed, PR #2257) and #2013 (closed-completed, PR #2015) in #2506, #1970 (closed-completed, PR #1981) in #2508. In two of the three cases the fix that closed the issue is the very mechanism the new issue proposes to build, and in the #2013 case the root cause is a host-side untimed Permission.ask deferred that no plugin-side watchdog can reach.
- wsG: Both audit findings the parent flagged sit directly under this workstream and neither is mentioned anywhere in it. HOOKS-2 (HIGH, critic UPHELD) is the exact brake #2507 wants to build: `if (tool !== 'Task') return;` at src/hooks/guardrails/tool-before.ts:1719 and again `if (toolName !== 'Task')` at src/hooks/loop-detector.ts:28, against the host's `const id = "task"` (anomalyco/opencode@v1.18.3 packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:24) - a 3x warning and 5x 'CIRCUIT BREAKER' that have never fired, pinned green by 34 'Task' literals in src/hooks/loop-detector.test.ts. #2507 names no tool identifier at all, so nothing in it says the new breaker would be wired to the real one. And the lane-lock liveness blindness underlies #2506, #2508 and #2509's lane-liveness view: I verified at runtime (bun, real acquireLaneLocks in a tmpdir) 'acquired: true / listActiveLocks immediately: 1 / listActiveLocks after expiry: 0 / proper-lockfile still held: true', because the sidecar expiresAt is stamped once at acquisition (src/parallel/file-locks.ts:193, written only at :454) and never renewed while proper-lockfile refreshes the lock by mtime. Four consumers read that signal: src/hooks/init-orphan-recovery.ts:283, src/turbo/lean/phase-ready.ts:489, src/turbo/lean/task-completion.ts:251, src/services/swarm-residue.ts:159. Nothing in Workstreams A-G appears to own either defect.
- wsG: The workstream imports an architecture this plugin deliberately rejected. Upstream's watchdog is a setInterval poller (src/watchdog.ts:59, checkIntervalMs 60s), its breaker is an unbounded module-level Map keyed by team (src/tools/team-spawn.ts:13), its rate limiter is one process-global bucket (src/index.ts:141), and its dashboard listens on all interfaces with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and no auth (src/dashboard.ts:219, :427). Against that, this repository's execution-stall detector states the rule outright at src/hooks/guardrails/execution-stall.ts:40-42: 'There are no timers - invariant 1 forbids background work on the plugin, and a timer would keep the process alive.' Invariant 8 requires explicit eviction on module-level maps, and invariant 9 requires circuits keyed by session/invocation/action-digest. For four of five capabilities the honest ADR answer in #2505 is 'reimplement', which would make G1 a short note rather than a gating PR - and would also make G2-G4 estimable, because they would be described against this codebase instead of against upstream's.
- wsG: Three of the five issues depend on Workstream D and only one says so. #2508 correctly declares D2 -> #2481 for its confirm-token store. #2509 renders gate/circuit/lane/delegation state that today does not exist in swarm.db (four tables: project_constraints, qa_gate_profile, qa_gate_profile_identity, task_checkpoint_receipt at src/db/project-db.ts:30-163) and declares only D1 -> #2480, whose own scope is 'low-risk caches, receipts, and checkpoints'. #2507 mentions D2 only as an edge case. As sequenced, G5 cannot begin when G4 ends.
- wsG: Two of the five (#2506's watchdog shutdown and #2509's listener shutdown) require a plugin `dispose` hook that does not exist - grep for 'dispose' in src/index.ts returns nothing, which is audit MAIN-1 (HIGH) and INIT-8 (MEDIUM), and no issue in Workstreams A-G appears to own it. Both issues promise lifecycle behaviour that has no host-invoked teardown point today.
- wsG: Every issue carries the same boilerplate closure contract ('Ships a docs/releases/pending/.md fragment'). For #2505, a docs-only ADR, the repository's own gate disagrees: scripts/check-pending-fragment.ts:41-56 counts only src/, bin/, binaries/, runners/, .github/workflows/, the three skill trees, package.json and docs/configuration.md as user-visible, and audit DOCS-10 already reports 595 consumed fragments accumulating in docs/releases/pending with no pruning step.
- wsG: Line-anchor hygiene is good and I confirmed it: every issue says 'Validated against: main @ 65be8637 (v7.162.1)'. That commit exists, and `git diff 832ce52 65be8637` over the files I cited (file-locks.ts, init-orphan-recovery.ts, loop-detector.ts, tool-before.ts, worktree/merge.ts, project-db.ts, registry.ts, url-security.ts, gate-denial-tracker.ts, execution-stall.ts, config/schema.ts, turbo/lean/runner.ts) shows no changes, so my citations hold at the roadmap's own baseline. The exception is src/hooks/pr-workflow-gate.ts, partly decomposed into src/pr-review/** by ae7fc72b; settlePresumedStalePrWorkflowLanes is still there at line 2644 in 65be8637 with unchanged behaviour.

Findings merged during verification, reported once under the canonical id:

- ROADNEW-2 is the same defect as PARALLEL-1. Both describe the same defect: lean_turbo's phase_critic gate is default-true while runState.lastCriticVerdict has no production writer and dispatchPhaseCritic has only test callers. The audit lane found it independently of the roadmap issue. Report it once, under PARALLEL-1, and record that #2470 owns it.
- testsci-1-NEW-1 is the same defect as TESTSCI-8. Same defect and the same two evidence lines: the merge-queue integration loop and the coverage gate call bun test directly, so a synchronous or top-level-await hang runs to the job budget instead of exiting 124 as the unit job wrapper does. Report once under TESTSCI-8.
- config-1-NEW-1 is the same defect as CONFIG-3. Restates the finding its author was verifying. CONFIG-3 already enumerates the two modes.md fences among its five failing config samples and records running the loader on the same sample. The one element outside CONFIG-3 was itself wrong.
- TOOLS-1 is the same defect as HOST-1. Same defect, and c14 established that HOST-1's framing is the correct one for this plugin. TOOLS-1's 'additive-only, an explicit false still denies' holds only for agents authored in a configuration file, which pass through the host's decoder; opencode-swarm has no such agents, since the installer writes two disable flags and nothing else. For all 21 plugin-injected agents the map is inert. Report once under HOST-1, and state the fix as emitting a permission block rather than rewriting the permissive entries. The report-level critic ruled on this directly: critic batch c14 is a gate of the same kind as c04, later, and holding a runtime replay c04 did not have; it retracted c04's mechanism and said the two findings must be merged. Merging therefore honours the later gate rather than overriding the earlier one, and leaving the entry would preserve a verdict the gate itself withdrew. Merged in section 3 as well as in the coverage count.

- #2115 run-memory is a read-only subsystem: nothing ever writes .swarm/run-memory.jsonl — The main claim is correctly retired (src/services/run-memory.ts:169 documents itself as 'the single production producer'), but the residual the comment defers — 'skip/retry outcome asymmetry' — is routed to '[Workstream D] PR 3' which does not list #2115 and has no bullet for it.
- #2273 Track post-merge follow-ups from PR #2261 review — A multi-item follow-up tracker collapsed into #2476 with no itemisation. #2476's closure contract says it 'closes a source issue only if its complete validated scope is satisfied' — but nobody can evaluate that condition because the items were never transcribed into #2476.
- #1248 PR #1194 — Follow-up work items (post-review) — Same pattern: 'Finish only the still-live #1248 items' in #2479 without saying which are still live, so the acceptance gate is unevaluable and any dropped item is unrecoverable from the roadmap alone.
- #1028 CI invariant checks: address advisory findings from council review — '#1028 advisory findings close here' in #2479 with no enumeration of the findings.

(docs/releases/pending/ (602 .md at 65be8637))
- #1896: "residual circuit/recovery diagnostics (fixed ACCEPTANCE/quota-failover parts stay closed)" — in fact The quota-failover half is not fixed in the sense the comment implies. src/index.ts:3906 gates registerPendingTaskModelRoute on an exact 'Task' compare while the host emits 'task' and normalizeToolName does not case-fold (src/hooks/normalize-tool-name.ts:26), so no task-model route is ever registered and the fallback chain plus the MODEL_FALLBACK_EXHAUSTED preflight are unreachable (audit HOOKS-3, critic UPHELD; corroborated by OBSERVABILITY-3). #2471 repeats the premise: 'Complete remaining #1896 sandbox-wrapper/circuit recovery diagnostics without reopening fixed quota failover.' (src/index.ts:3906 ; src/hooks/normalize-tool-name.ts:26 ; src/index.ts:4091)

- Reconciliation is clean at the ledger level. All 97 issues open in the pre-re-baseline snapshot are now closed. 92 were closed inside the 02:16-02:36 window; the other five (#1537, #1603, #1964, #2045, #2445) were closed earlier the same evening by genuinely merged PRs (#2460, #2459, #2458, #2461, #2453) and are not part of the re-baseline. Nothing was left open, and no issue outside the snapshot was swept up.
- 91 of the 92 window closures carry a re-baseline comment; the 92nd (#2385) was closed at 02:36 by merged PR #2462 with a detailed closeout and three properly-filed residual issues (#2510, #2511, #2512). #2510's factual claim was independently verified: no pathGrammar row covers .swarm/pr-workflow-gates/*.json at 65be8637, only the EXEMPT_WRITER_MODULES text at scripts/retention-registry.data.ts:3580 mentions the gap.
- Every roadmap issue named as a consolidation target exists and is open. There are no dangling or self-closed targets. 84 of the 92 closures name a target by issue number; the other 8 name a workstream and PR position in prose only (#2449, #2386 -> 'Workstream C PR 2'; #2184, #2115 -> 'Workstream D PR 3'; #2143, #1943 -> 'Workstream C PR 1'; #1665 -> 'Workstream F PR 3'; #1693 -> 'Workstream A PR 2/PR 3').
- The reverse mapping is where fidelity leaks. Six issues whose closure comment names a target are NOT listed in that target's own 'Source issues' line: #1823 (names #2482, listed only in #2487), #2115 (names D3/#2482, listed nowhere), #1643 (names F1/#2493, listed nowhere), #2143, #1943 and #1693 (all closed as resolved, listed nowhere). Since each roadmap issue's closure contract says it 'closes a source issue only if its complete validated scope is satisfied', a scope that never entered the Source list can be satisfied without anyone noticing the omission.
- The 12 'Auto-detected flaky tests (merge-group)' bot issues (#2449, #2416, #2386, #2368, #2330, #2322, #2305, #2235, #2143, #2028, #2017, #1943) were checked as a group rather than individually. Ten map cleanly into #2477 or #2478, which name the specific flake families (council-quorum, knowledge-query, dispatch-lanes, evaluation-runner, gate-utils, plan-sync, phase-complete, skill_improver quota) and carry a soak exit criterion relocated from tracker #1782. The two exceptions are #2143 (dup, root-fix PR #2190 cited) and #1943 (no evidence cited at all).
- The roadmap bodies are, with the exceptions listed in falseClaims, unusually accurate about the codebase. Every line-cited claim I sampled held: src/telemetry.ts:298 pins the first project (verified :297-300); src/db/project-db.ts:212 keys the connection cache on a lexical resolve(); install() disables only explore/general and never sets auto_select_architect (src/cli/index.ts:320-352, src/config/schema.ts:3439); src/commands/turbo.ts:248 falls through to a toggle on an unknown argument; src/council/web-search-provider.ts:88 and :153 call fetch with no signal; binaries/win32-x64 and win32-arm64 contain only .gitkeep and release-and-publish.yml has zero cargo steps; the 14-byte UTF-16 file.txt exists at the repo root; src/graph/ has indeed been deleted; bun.lock carries both zod@4.1.8 and zod@4.3.6; and scripts/retention-registry.data.ts really does hold 108 pathGrammar rows at 65be8637, as #2483 claims. This is a materially higher standard than the false #2436 comment set.
- The structural failure is coverage, not bookkeeping. The re-baseline was built from the previously-open issue set, so it inherits that set's blind spots: 11 of the 19 verified HIGH/CRITICAL audit findings — MAIN-10, HOOKS-7, HOOKS-1, HOOKS-2, HOOKS-3, PLAN-1, PLAN-2, PLAN-3, PLAN-4, SECURITY-1, TOOLS-1 — are not addressed by any of the 44 issues, and 6 more are only partly addressed. Two subsystems the audit found most broken (the plan projection/ledger correctness family, and system-message delivery to the model) have no roadmap presence at all: the only plan issue, #2484, migrates the ledger to SQLite while explicitly preserving current semantics.
- #2471 and the #1896 closure both assert the quota-failover defect is fixed, which is the one place the re-baseline actively records a wrong state rather than merely omitting one. Anyone reading the tracker now believes model failover on quota exhaustion works; src/index.ts:3906 says it never registers a route.
- Closing multi-item trackers into a single roadmap bullet is the most common fidelity loss. #2273, #1248, #1028, #2184 and #1823 were each collapsed into a one-line reference ('post-#2261 hardening follow-ups', 'Finish only the still-live #1248 items', '#1028 advisory findings close here') with no itemisation. Each roadmap issue's closure contract makes the source issue's closure conditional on 'its complete validated scope', but that scope now exists only in the closed issue's body — reachable, but no longer in any acceptance gate.
- #2046 is closed while its fix is in an open, unmerged PR (#2466), and #1643 likewise (#2329). Both rely on a PR landing that nothing gates. This sits uneasily with the project's own directive 1 ('we never defer work ... a deferred task whose output is consumed must be observable and verifiable').
- Workstream G (#2505-#2509, opencode-ensemble adoption) consolidates no closed issue at all — it is five net-new issues. It is also the only workstream with a license-compliance gate (#2505) blocking the other four, which is well constructed.

Required before merge:

- Fix the check:test-clock failure: route the new waitFor deadline through the repo's freezeClock/withFrozenClock helper (or import it in tests/unit/background/plan-sync-worker.test.ts) and re-run `bun run check:test-clock`. This is currently red in CI and is the reason unit is skipped and unit-passed fails.
- Fix the six check:test-file-cap ratchet violations before the first gate is fixed — otherwise the build simply fails one step later. Split the added behaviour out of the six over-cap files (the new waitFor and the plan-sync teardown belong in a sibling file; the legacy-oracle additions push a file from exactly 500 to 553), or take an explicit, reviewed TEST_CAP_ENFORCE=0 exemption and say so in the body.
- Correct the PR body's invariant-7 audit: 'check:test-file-cap: 0 violations' is false (6 ratchet violations), and the audit omits check:test-clock, the gate that is actually failing.
- Either drop 'Closes #2477' or re-scope the issue's soak exit criterion. As written, merging closes an issue whose own stated close-the-loop evidence ('a merge-group window with zero new auto-filed flake issues after these fixes') cannot exist until after the merge.
- Fix the circular quarantine exit criterion for tests/unit/commands/pr-monitor-status.test.ts, or state in the entry that TESTSCI-2 (quarantined files are excluded from the very windows-latest merge-group runs the criterion requires) blocks retirement and name the issue that owns it.
- Migrate the two pkg-audit composer files' own teardown to createSafeTestDir / retried safeRmRecursive, matching what this PR does to every other Windows-flaky file it touches.
- Recommended, not blocking: since this is the CI-stability PR, extend the integration job's find at ci.yml:789 beyond -maxdepth 1 (69 tests in tests/integration/lang are run by no CI job) and anchor the detect-release predicate at ci.yml:56, or file and link the issues that own them so they are not silently carried into C2/C3.

Cross-PR observations:

- Both PRs are first-of-workstream and both landed within hours of the 44-issue roadmap being filed, with the same author, the same body template (Summary / Invariant audit / Test plan) and the same self-reported multi-model review chain. The template is genuinely load-bearing — the 12-invariant audits are specific and mostly accurate — but neither body's validation section is trustworthy on its own: 2514 claims 'check:test-file-cap: 0 violations' where the gate reports 6, and omits the one gate that is red in CI; 2515 claims a largest new test file of 227 lines where it is 269. In both cases the false claims are in the section a reviewer would use to skip re-running the gates.
- The roadmap's declared dependency graph is not being honoured. #2480 states 'Dependencies (resolved) - B1 -> #2474', but #2474 is open with no linked PR, and its scope explicitly owns 'project-db.ts:212-227 connection cache keys (currently lexical resolve())' — precisely what PR 2515 implements in a new, DB-scoped helper whose own header concedes B1 owns the repo-wide rollout. D1 is therefore shipping B1's work first and creating a second identity helper that B1 must later reconcile. 'Dependencies (resolved)' appears to be a template line rather than a verified state.
- The two PRs' verification surfaces sit almost entirely inside the merge queue, which the audit has already shown to be the weakest link. On the pull_request tier both PRs have integration, smoke, package-check, security and coverage-shard skipped; PR 2515's only real-Node, three-OS proof (repro:1873) runs solely in the merge-group smoke job, and that job is gated on the unanchored detect-release grep that can mark an ordinary PR as a release and turn every step into a no-op with the check still green. A foundation PR of 5,280 added lines is being validated by a pipeline whose decisive leg is one unpinned regex away from not running.
- PR 2514 is the CI-and-test-stability PR of Workstream C and fixes one of the five testing defects the audit verified. tsconfig still excludes tests/ and scripts/, biome still ignores scripts/ (it literally answered 'These paths were provided but ignored' for the two gate scripts this PR rewrites), the integration job's find still uses -maxdepth 1 so 69 tests in tests/integration/lang run nowhere, and the release predicate is untouched. The class it does close — a mock.module delegation that becomes an unkillable tail-recursive loop — it closes properly: I reproduced the mechanism from scratch (a hand-written namespace-spread delegation hung a bun test process until my 90 s kill) and confirmed the new gate rule flags that file. Good root-cause work, aimed at a narrower target than the workstream's title implies.
- PR 2515's engineering quality is materially higher than its issue's framing suggests, and the gap is in the enumeration, not the code. Its migrations, group-commit transaction discipline, canonical-identity cache, durability escalation and retention-registry redesign are all real and tested (60 tests in tests/unit/db, 360 across all 38 changed test files in one process, repro:1873 green under real Node). What it misses is the one Bun/Node divergence the audit had already proven: the PR builds a 'driver-parity contract' as a named acceptance criterion, enumerates the SQLITE_RANGE parameter-count delta in code and in docs/engineering-invariants.md, exercises the exact no-argument run() path in the contract, and never looks at that call's return value — which is a Changes object under Bun and undefined under the Node adapter, and which /swarm memory unlink dereferences today. It then extends the real-Node harness barrel with seven new exports without adding the function that would expose it. A contract is only as good as the deltas someone remembered to write down, and this one canonised an incomplete list.
- Both PRs put substantial weight on 'no unwired code' in their bodies while shipping unwired code. 2515 ships a dead export (closeAllGroupCommitWriters, zero call sites anywhere), a write-only artefact (.swarm/db-migration-failure.json has a producer, a deleter, documentation and no reader — in exactly the v14-failure case where the in-DB alternative cannot exist), and a new plugin dispose hook with no test. 2514 documents a post-merge soak protocol as its issue's closure evidence while using 'Closes #2477'. The permanent CLAUDE.md directive calls dead exports and untested new code paths blockers rather than follow-ups; the roadmap's own closure contract repeats it in every issue. That the same author's PRs violate it twice suggests the contract is being copied into issues faster than it is being applied to diffs.

## 8. Appendix: artifacts

Explorer maps, findings JSON, GitHub inventory (issues and PRs as JSONL), CHANGELOG analyses, probe scripts and harnesses, reviewer verdict files and critic decision files were written under the session scratchpad (`scratchpad/maps`, `scratchpad/findings`, `scratchpad/gh`, `scratchpad/perf`, `scratchpad/portability`, `scratchpad/state-census`, `scratchpad/journey-project`, `scratchpad/verify/{batches,verdicts,critic,critic-batches}`). They are not committed. The reviewer and critic briefs are `scratchpad/verify/REVIEWER_BRIEF.md` and `scratchpad/verify/CRITIC_BRIEF.md`.
